# Shadleaf

> shadcn/ui for Thymeleaf, as a Spring Boot starter. The complete documentation.

Shadleaf 0.11.0-SNAPSHOT.

## Shadleaf

> shadcn/ui for Thymeleaf, as a Spring Boot starter.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/

Shadleaf brings the [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com) design system to Thymeleaf. Add one dependency, include two
fragments in your layout's `<head>`, and write `<sl:button>`:

**Example: Variants.**

```html
<sl:button>Default</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="outline">Outline</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="ghost">Ghost</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="destructive">Destructive</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="secondary">Secondary</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="link">Link</sl:button>
```

- **Fits your build.** The jar ships compiled CSS, served under `/shadleaf/**`, so a plain Maven build is enough.
  Already compiling Tailwind? The [embedded bundle](guides/tailwind/) fits into your own
  build.
- **shadcn's token names, verbatim.** `--primary`, `--radius`, `--ring`: any shadcn theme drops in unchanged.
- **Declared props.** A typo such as `variant="destructve"` fails with the legal values, and an icon-only button
  without an `aria-label` fails too, instead of shipping.
- **Adjustable in five steps**, from a prop to owning the template yourself: see
  [the adjustability ladder](guides/adjustability/).
- **Works under a strict Content-Security-Policy**, with no `'unsafe-inline'`: see [CSP](guides/csp/).

Every preview on this site is rendered by the library itself, from the build that produced these pages, so it shows
exactly the markup your application gets.

> **Caution: Pre-release**
>
> Before 1.0, the rendered markup, class names and `data-*` attributes can change between versions.

---

## Getting started

> Add Shadleaf to a Spring Boot application.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/getting-started/

Shadleaf needs Java 17, Spring Boot 4 and Thymeleaf. The jar ships compiled CSS and JavaScript, so a plain Maven
build is enough to get started.

### Add the dependency

Add the dependency to your `pom.xml` of your Spring Boot with Thymeleaf application:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.github.wimdeblauwe</groupId>
  <artifactId>shadleaf-spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
  <version>0.11.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
</dependency>
```

> **Note: Don't have an application yet?**
>
> You can generate an application from [Spring Initializr](https://start.spring.io/) with the Spring Web & Thymeleaf dependencies.
>
> Alternatively, use [ttcli](https://github.com/wimdeblauwe/ttcli) to generate an application.
> It allows to have a very nice live-reload setup for quick development.

### Include the stylesheet and the theme script

In the `<head>` of your layout:

```html
<head>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: theme-script}"></th:block>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: assets}"></th:block>
  <!-- your own stylesheet after it, so your overrides win -->
  <link rel="stylesheet" th:href="@{/css/application.css}">
</head>
```

The `theme-script` reads the user's preference from `localStorage` and sets the `class="dark"` on `<html>` before the first paint.
Place the [`<sl:theme-toggle>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/theme-toggle.md) on your page to let the user choose between light and dark mode.

The `assets` block renders the CSS and JS links.
By default, Alpine.js is loaded and you can use it in your own pages.
See [Alpine.js](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/alpine.md) if your application loads Alpine itself.

If you want to use Tailwind CSS in your own pages, see [Tailwind CSS](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tailwind.md) for how to set it up.

If you have a Content-Security-Policy, see [CSP](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/csp.md) for more information.

### Use the components

Add a component to your Thymeleaf template:

```html
<html xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl">
...
<sl:button variant="outline">Cancel</sl:button>
<sl:button type="submit">Save</sl:button>
```

See the [Components](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components.md) section for all available components and their attributes.
There are also [Layouts](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts.md) with whole page layouts to copy.

### Configuration

| Property                       | Default      |                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|--------------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `shadleaf.skin`                | `vega`       | The visual identity, named after the shadcn/ui style it follows; see [Skin](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/adjustability.md#4-skin) for the list.                                                       |
| `shadleaf.assets.variant`      | `standalone` | `embedded` leaves out Tailwind's reset, for applications that compile Tailwind themselves.                                                                                       |
| `shadleaf.assets.alpine`       | `bundled`    | Where Alpine.js comes from: `bundled`, `csp` or `external`; see [Alpine.js](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/alpine.md).                                                                                  |
| `shadleaf.csp.nonce-attribute` | `cspNonce`   | The request attribute holding a CSP nonce for the theme script.                                                                                                                  |
| `shadleaf.security.login-url`  | `/login`     | Where the user menu's Sign in link goes; `/oauth2/authorization/<id>` with one OAuth2 login client. See [Spring Security](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/spring-security.md#sign-in-and-sign-out-urls). |
| `shadleaf.security.logout-url` | `/logout`    | Where the user menu's sign-out form posts to; see [Spring Security](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/spring-security.md#sign-in-and-sign-out-urls).                                                       |
| `shadleaf.dev.web-types-file`  |              | Writes IDE metadata for your components; see [IDE completion](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/ide-completion.md).                                                                                               |

---

## Coming from shadcn/ui

> What carries over from shadcn/ui unchanged, and where Shadleaf differs, and why.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/coming-from-shadcn/

Most of what you know from shadcn/ui carries over. The component and part names map one to one
(`CardHeader` is `<sl:card-header>`), and so do the variant and size names (`variant="outline" size="sm"`). The colour
tokens are shadcn's, verbatim: a theme from tweakcn or the shadcn theme generator drops in unchanged. Porting an example
is mostly a matter of renaming tags.

The skins are shadcn's styles too, all eight of them: `shadleaf.skin=vega` (the default), `nova`, `maia`, `lyra`,
`mira`, `luma`, `sera` and `rhea`; [Skin](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/adjustability.md#4-skin) lists them. One more is Shadleaf's own:
`sketch`, which looks hand-drawn, for mockups.

This page lists where Shadleaf differs. Some differences come from running on the server with Thymeleaf instead of in
React; the others are deliberate, mostly for accessibility.

### Because it is Thymeleaf, not React

#### `as` instead of `asChild`

There is no `asChild`. A component that can render as a link takes `as="a"`:

```html
<!-- shadcn: <Button asChild><a href="/orders">Orders</a></Button> -->
<sl:button as="a" th:href="@{/orders}">Orders</sl:button>
```

#### No utility classes in the library's CSS

shadcn styles its components with Tailwind classes compiled into your application. Shadleaf ships its own stylesheet,
which defines no utility classes, so it works in an application that does not compile Tailwind at all. Where a shadcn
example relies on a utility class to change a component, Shadleaf has a prop instead:

| shadcn/ui | Shadleaf |
| --- | --- |
| `<CardHeader className="border-b">` | `<sl:card-header border>` |
| `<Empty className="border border-dashed">` | `<sl:empty border>` |
| `<Spinner className="size-8" />` | `<sl:spinner size="32"/>` |
| `<Attachment className="w-full">` | `<sl:attachment full-width>` |
| `<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />` | `<sl:skeleton/>` (a line is the default), `shape="circle"` for an avatar |

Your own classes still work: `class` is appended to the component's own, so `class="w-64"` sizes a skeleton when your
application compiles Tailwind. See [the adjustability ladder](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/adjustability.md).

#### The avatar decides on the server

shadcn's avatar renders the image only once it has loaded in the browser, and the fallback until then. Shadleaf
always renders both, and the stylesheet picks one: the fallback when the image has no `src` or an empty one, which is
what `th:src` gives for a user without a photo, needs no script at all. For a photo that is loading or fails to load,
Shadleaf's script marks the image `data-status="loaded"` or `"error"` (where Radix has `onLoadingStatusChange`), and the
fallback shows until it is loaded, as in shadcn. There is no `delayMs`. Without JavaScript the image simply lies over
the fallback.

#### Dialogs open with invoker commands

A dialog is the browser's `<dialog>` element, so `DialogContent`, `DialogOverlay` and `DialogPortal` are all
`<sl:dialog>`. There is no `DialogTrigger` or `DialogClose`, and no `open`/`onOpenChange` state: every dialog has an
`id`, and any button opens or closes it with `commandfor` and `command`:

```html
<!-- shadcn: <DialogTrigger asChild><Button variant="outline">Edit</Button></DialogTrigger> -->
<sl:button variant="outline" commandfor="edit-profile" command="show-modal">Edit</sl:button>
<!-- shadcn: <DialogClose asChild><Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button></DialogClose> -->
<sl:button variant="outline" commandfor="edit-profile" command="close">Cancel</sl:button>
```

`open` on `<sl:dialog>` opens it when it is rendered (for a dialog htmx fetches), and the server closes it with the
`sl-dialog-close` event. The title is a `div` with `role="heading"` and `aria-level="2"` (Radix renders an `h2`), so
an application's own `h2` styles do not reach it. Content taller than the screen scrolls inside the dialog. See
[Dialog](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/dialog.md).

#### Alert dialog: a cancel part, no action part

`<sl:alert-dialog>` is the same `<dialog>` element with `role="alertdialog"`, opened the same way, and a click
outside does not close it. `AlertDialogCancel` is `<sl:alert-dialog-cancel>`: it closes the dialog, takes the focus
when it opens (as Radix's Cancel does) and says "Cancel" unless you give it text. `AlertDialogAction` has no part: in a
server-rendered page the action submits a form or sends an htmx request, so it is a plain `<sl:button>`:

```html
<!-- shadcn: <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel> -->
<sl:alert-dialog-cancel/>
<!-- shadcn: <AlertDialogAction variant="destructive">Delete</AlertDialogAction> -->
<sl:button variant="destructive" type="submit">Delete</sl:button>
```

shadcn's destructive example colours the media with `className="bg-destructive/10 text-destructive"`; Shadleaf has
`<sl:alert-dialog-media variant="destructive">`. See [Alert Dialog](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/alert-dialog.md).

#### Sheet: content padding, and sides that follow the text direction

`<sl:sheet>` is a dialog on an edge of the screen, with `SheetTrigger` and `SheetClose` replaced by `commandfor`, as
for the dialog. Content between the header and the footer gets the sheet's inline padding, where shadcn's examples
wrap it in a `div` with `px-4`. `side="right"` and `"left"` are the end and the start of a line, so they swap on a
right-to-left page. `<sl:sheet-footer show-close-button>` adds an outline Close button, as the dialog footer does. With
reduced motion the sheet only fades. See [Sheet](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sheet.md).

#### Dialog and sheet bodies: an addition for htmx

shadcn has no body part. `<sl:dialog-body>` and `<sl:sheet-body>` are Shadleaf's own: the content between the header
and the footer, which scrolls by itself, and the target for htmx. A request into it opens the dialog or sheet at once,
shows a spinner until the answer is in, and reports a failure as a toast or in the dialog. Without a body, the content
goes straight into the dialog, as in shadcn. See [Dialog](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/dialog.md#loaded-into-the-dialog-a-body).

#### Dropdown menu, popover and tooltip are popovers

The three are the browser's [popovers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API), placed next to
their trigger with CSS anchor positioning, so there are no portals and no `open`/`onOpenChange` state.
`<sl:dropdown-menu>` and `<sl:popover>` render no element of their own and need an `id`; the trigger part is a
`<sl:button>` with `popovertarget`, and any other button opens them with `popovertarget` too:

```html
<!-- shadcn: <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild><Button variant="outline">Open</Button></DropdownMenuTrigger> -->
<sl:dropdown-menu-trigger variant="outline">Open</sl:dropdown-menu-trigger>
```

`asChild` around a sidebar part is `as` on the trigger, which renders that part with the menu's attributes:

```html
<!-- shadcn: <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild><SidebarMenuButton size="lg">…</SidebarMenuButton></DropdownMenuTrigger> -->
<sl:dropdown-menu-trigger as="sidebar-menu-button" size="lg">…</sl:dropdown-menu-trigger>
<!-- shadcn: <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild><SidebarMenuAction showOnHover>…</SidebarMenuAction></DropdownMenuTrigger> -->
<sl:dropdown-menu-trigger as="sidebar-menu-action" show-on-hover aria-label="More for Design">…</sl:dropdown-menu-trigger>
```

- A menu item is a button or, with `as="a"`, a link; there is no `onSelect`. It does what its attributes say (`href`,
  `hx-*`, `type="submit"`, `commandfor`) and the menu closes.
- Checkbox and radio items show the state the server renders (`checked`); there is no `onCheckedChange` or `value`.
  Choosing one sends a request, and the page that comes back shows the new state.
- No sub-menus, no `DropdownMenuPortal`, no `modal`. See [Dropdown menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/dropdown-menu.md#left-out).
- No `PopoverAnchor`. A form in a popover can close it with an `HX-Trigger: sl-popover-close` response header. See
  [Popover](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/popover.md).
- There is no `TooltipTrigger` and no `TooltipProvider`: the first element inside `<sl:tooltip>` is the trigger, and
  `delay` sits on each tooltip. See [Tooltip](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/tooltip.md).
- `side="right"` and `"left"` are the end and the start of a line, as for the sheet.

#### Select is a real select

`<sl:select>` renders a `<select>`, so `th:field` binds it and the form submits it without a hidden input. The
customizable select (`appearance: base-select`) draws its list where the browser has it (Chrome and Edge 135, Safari
27); elsewhere a small Alpine component shows a list box in its place, and without Alpine it is the browser's own
select.

```html
<!-- shadcn: <Select><SelectTrigger><SelectValue placeholder="Select a fruit"/></SelectTrigger>
             <SelectContent><SelectGroup><SelectLabel>Fruits</SelectLabel>
             <SelectItem value="apple">Apple</SelectItem>... -->
<sl:select th:field="*{fruit}" placeholder="Select a fruit">
  <sl:select-group label="Fruits">
    <sl:select-item value="apple">Apple</sl:select-item>
  </sl:select-group>
</sl:select>
```

- `SelectTrigger`, `SelectValue` and `SelectContent` are all `<sl:select>`: `size` and `placeholder` are its props.
- A group's heading is `<sl:select-group label>`; there is no `SelectLabel` part.
- No scroll buttons, no `position="item-aligned"`, `side` or `align`: the list opens below the select, or above it
  when there is no room.
- No `value`/`onValueChange`: `th:field` renders the value, and the select fires `change`.
- The keyboard is the browser's where it draws the list: typing a letter on the closed select chooses the matching
  item at once, as on any select, where Radix opens the list. See [Select](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/select.md#left-out).

#### Combobox is a real select too

`<sl:combobox>` renders a `<select>` (a `<select multiple>` with `multiple`) holding its items, so `th:field` binds
one value or a collection and the form submits them without a hidden input. A small Alpine component puts the input,
the chips and the list box in its place; without Alpine it is a select drawn like the native select.

```html
<!-- shadcn: <Combobox items={frameworks}><ComboboxInput placeholder="Select a framework" showClear/>
             <ComboboxContent><ComboboxEmpty>No items found.</ComboboxEmpty><ComboboxList>
             {(item) => <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>}</ComboboxList>
             </ComboboxContent></Combobox> -->
<sl:combobox th:field="*{framework}" placeholder="Select a framework" show-clear>
  <sl:combobox-item th:each="framework : ${frameworks}" th:value="${framework.id}">[[${framework.name}]]</sl:combobox-item>
</sl:combobox>

<!-- shadcn: <Combobox multiple ...><ComboboxChips><ComboboxValue>{...<ComboboxChip/>}</ComboboxValue>
             <ComboboxChipsInput/></ComboboxChips>... -->
<sl:combobox th:field="*{frameworks}" multiple placeholder="Add a framework">...</sl:combobox>
```

- `ComboboxInput`, `ComboboxContent`, `ComboboxList`, `ComboboxChips`, `ComboboxChip`, `ComboboxChipsInput`,
  `ComboboxValue` and `ComboboxTrigger` are all `<sl:combobox>`: `showClear`, `showTrigger` and `autoHighlight` are
  its `show-clear`, `show-trigger` and `auto-highlight`, and `ComboboxEmpty` is its `empty` attribute.
- No `items` array or render function: the items are `<sl:combobox-item>`s, whose `value` and text replace
  `itemToStringValue`. A group's heading is `<sl:combobox-group label>`; there is no `ComboboxLabel` or
  `ComboboxCollection`.
- An addition: `search-url` loads the options from the server as you type, as an HTML fragment of items.
- No popup layout (a button trigger with the input in the list), no input addons, no `showRemove` on a chip, no
  `side`/`align`. See [Combobox](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/combobox.md#left-out).

#### Toggle and toggle group are checkboxes and radio buttons

`<sl:toggle>` is a checkbox drawn as a button, and the items of `<sl:toggle-group>` are radio buttons
(`type="single"`) or checkboxes (`type="multiple"`). So `th:field` binds them, the form submits them, and they work
without JavaScript; a screen reader announces a toggle as a checkbox, checked or not, where Radix's is a toggle button,
pressed or not.

```html
<!-- shadcn: <Toggle aria-label="Toggle italic" defaultPressed><Italic/></Toggle> -->
<sl:toggle name="italic" aria-label="Toggle italic" checked><sl:icon name="italic"/></sl:toggle>

<!-- shadcn: <ToggleGroup type="single" variant="outline" defaultValue="grid">
             <ToggleGroupItem value="list">List</ToggleGroupItem>... -->
<sl:toggle-group th:field="*{layout}" variant="outline" aria-label="Layout">
  <sl:toggle-group-item value="list">List</sl:toggle-group-item>
  <sl:toggle-group-item value="grid">Grid</sl:toggle-group-item>
</sl:toggle-group>
```

- No `pressed`/`defaultPressed`/`onPressedChange`, nor `value`/`defaultValue`/`onValueChange` on the group:
  `checked` (or `th:field`) renders the state, and the inputs fire `change`.
- The group takes the `th:field` or `name` its items share; Radix's has neither.
- The keyboard is the browser's: in a `single` group the arrow keys move between the items and select them, and Tab
  leaves the group; in a `multiple` group every item is a tab stop. Radix's arrow keys only move the focus, in both
  types. There is no `loop` or `rovingFocus`.
- A `single` group cannot be cleared by clicking its item again, as a radio button cannot.
- `spacing` takes `0` to `4`, and `variant` and `size` are set on the group only, not per item.

#### Calendar is drawn over date inputs

`<sl:calendar>` holds its value in `<input type="date">` elements, so `th:field` binds it and the form submits ISO
dates. A small Alpine component draws the month over them; without Alpine the date inputs show.

```html
<!-- shadcn: <Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate}/> -->
<sl:calendar th:field="*{dueDate}"/>

<!-- shadcn: <Calendar mode="range" selected={range} onSelect={setRange} numberOfMonths={2}/> -->
<sl:calendar aria-label="Stay" number-of-months="2">
  <sl:input type="date" th:field="*{checkIn}" aria-label="Check-in"/>
  <sl:input type="date" th:field="*{checkOut}" aria-label="Check-out"/>
</sl:calendar>
```

- No `mode`: one date input is a single date, two (start and end) are a range. No `mode="multiple"` yet.
- No `selected`/`onSelect`: `th:field` renders the value, and the input fires `change`.
- `disabled` disables the whole calendar, as on an input; the days that cannot be picked are `disabled-dates`
  (`sat,sun,2026-12-24..2026-12-31`), plus the inputs' `min` and `max`.
- The page's locale sets the first day of the week and the week numbering; `week-starts-on` overrides the first day.
- No `timeZone`, `buttonVariant`, `classNames`, `components` or `formatters`. See
  [Calendar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/calendar.md#left-out).

#### Month view is a component

shadcn's Calendar shows content per day through react-day-picker's `components={{DayButton}}`, and full-month
calendars are blocks built on top of it. `<sl:month-view>` is a component of its own for that: rendered on the
server, no picking, a `day` slot per day and a link per day.

```html
<!-- shadcn: <Calendar components={{DayButton: ({children, modifiers, day, ...props}) => <CalendarDayButton
     day={day} modifiers={modifiers} {...props}>{children}<span>{events[day.date]}</span></CalendarDayButton>}}/> -->
<sl:month-view day-href="/agenda/{date}">
  <sl:slot name="day"><span th:text="${events[slDay.date]}"></span></sl:slot>
</sl:month-view>
```

- The previous and next month are links to the server (`?month=2026-09`), not client state.
- See [Month view](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/month-view.md).

#### Date picker is a component

shadcn has no date picker component: its docs compose a `Popover`, a `Button` and a `Calendar`, and the app's own
state updates the button and closes the popover. `<sl:date-picker>` is that composition as one component; its
attributes go to the calendar inside.

```html
<!-- shadcn: <Popover><PopoverTrigger asChild><Button variant="outline">{date ? format(date, "PPP") : "Pick a date"}
     </Button></PopoverTrigger><PopoverContent className="w-auto p-0" align="start">
     <Calendar mode="single" selected={date} onSelect={setDate}/></PopoverContent></Popover> -->
<sl:date-picker th:field="*{dueDate}"/>

<!-- shadcn: the same with <Calendar mode="range" numberOfMonths={2} .../> -->
<sl:date-picker aria-label="Stay" number-of-months="2">
  <sl:input type="date" th:field="*{checkIn}" aria-label="Check-in"/>
  <sl:input type="date" th:field="*{checkOut}" aria-label="Check-out"/>
</sl:date-picker>
```

- The button's text is formatted in the page's locale, by `format` (`Intl`'s `dateStyle`: `long` is close to
  date-fns' `PPP`), not by a date-fns pattern. A range shows both ends with ` – ` between them.
- A pick closes the popover: for a range, the second pick.
- It needs JavaScript; without it the popover holds the bare date inputs.
- The typed-input, time, natural language and presets demos have no counterpart yet.

#### Accordion and collapsible are details elements

Each accordion item and each collapsible is a `<details>` element with the trigger as its `<summary>`, so they need
no JavaScript. That changes a few things:

```html
<!-- shadcn: <Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="item-1">
             <AccordionItem value="item-1">... -->
<sl:accordion>
  <sl:accordion-item open>...</sl:accordion-item>
</sl:accordion>
```

- `defaultValue` is `open` on the item; items have no `value`, and there is no `onValueChange`.
- `type="single"` (the default here) is always `collapsible`: the browser lets the open `details` close. The items
  share a `name`, which must be unique on the page; one is generated when you give none.
- The trigger's text is a heading (`role="heading"`, `level`, 3 by default) inside the `summary`, where Radix puts the
  trigger's button in an `h3`.
- No arrow keys between accordion triggers (optional in the ARIA pattern): Tab moves between them.
- The trigger must be the first child of its item or collapsible; a collapsible's trigger cannot sit after its
  content. `<CollapsibleTrigger asChild><Button …>` is `<sl:collapsible-trigger variant="…" size="…">`.
- A closed disabled item renders no content, as Radix renders no closed content at all.

See [Accordion](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/accordion.md) and [Collapsible](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/collapsible.md).

#### Tabs: `tab` and `active` instead of `value` and `defaultValue`

`value` is taken in Thymeleaf (`th:value`), so a trigger and its panel share a `tab`, and `active` on `<sl:tabs>`
names the active one, which the server renders. The tabs need an `id`, and a trigger with an `href` is a link that
works without JavaScript:

```html
<!-- shadcn: <Tabs defaultValue="account"><TabsList><TabsTrigger value="account">... -->
<sl:tabs id="settings" active="account">
  <sl:tabs-list><sl:tabs-trigger tab="account">Account</sl:tabs-trigger>...</sl:tabs-list>
  <sl:tabs-content tab="account">...</sl:tabs-content>
</sl:tabs>
```

`activationMode` is `activation-mode`; there is no `onValueChange` (an `sl-tabs-show` event fires on the panel that is
shown). See [Tabs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/tabs.md).

#### Toast: the server sends the toasts

shadcn's toast is Sonner: a `<Toaster />` in the layout and `toast("...")` calls in the browser. Shadleaf has
`<sl:toaster>` in the layout, and the toasts come from the server: an htmx response sends the `sl-toast` event with
`HX-Trigger` (`htmxResponse.addTrigger("sl-toast", Toast.success("Saved"))`), a page renders `<sl:toast>`s from a flash
attribute after a redirect, or a response swaps them in out of band. A script can dispatch `sl-toast` itself, with the
same detail as Sonner's options: `{title, description, variant, duration}`. `toast.success()` and friends are the
`variant` (`success`, `info`, `warning`, `error`); `visibleToasts` is `visible-toasts`. See
[Toast](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/toast.md).

#### Theme toggle: a component, no `ThemeProvider`

shadcn's dark mode is next-themes: a `ThemeProvider` around the app and a `ModeToggle` you copy from the docs. Shadleaf
has the theme script in the layout's `<head>` (the provider's part: the `dark` class before the first paint) and
`<sl:theme-toggle/>`, the same menu with Light, Dark and System, its items checked by the current choice
(`menuitemradio`s; shadcn's are plain items). `as="button"` is the one-button switch of shadcn's own site. The choice
is stored under `localStorage['shadleaf-theme']` (next-themes uses `theme`), and System removes it. There is no
`useTheme()`: the `sl-theme-change` event tells a script about a change. See [Theme toggle](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/theme-toggle.md).

#### Table: plain rows and cells, sorted on the server

`<sl:table>` styles the plain table elements inside it, so there is no `TableHeader`, `TableBody`, `TableFooter`,
`TableRow`, `TableHead`, `TableCell` or `TableCaption`: write `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `th`, `td` and
`caption`, with `th:each` on the row. A page of 50 rows would otherwise be hundreds of components. Where shadcn's
data table sorts in the browser with TanStack Table, `<sl:table-head sort="name">` is a link that asks the server for
the page in another order (`?sort=name,desc`), read from a Spring Data `Page`. A cell's alignment is `data-align="end"`
rather than a `text-right` class. Filtering is a `GET` form the server answers, with `sl:query-params` keeping the
order and page size, and htmx to search as the user types ([Tables with htmx](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tables-htmx.md)). There is no
column visibility or browser-side paging. Row selection is the application's own checkboxes, which submit with a form:
`<sl:table-select-all>` takes the place of the header's `Checkbox` with `table.getIsAllPageRowsSelected()`, and
`<sl:table-selection-count>` of `"{n} of {total} row(s) selected."` (it reads "2 of 20 selected"). The selected row's
background comes from CSS (a checked checkbox in the row's first cell), not from `data-state="selected"`. The
selection covers the page only; a sort or another page starts afresh. See [Table](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md#selecting-rows).
The row actions are the same dropdown menu in the last cell, but its items post a form around the menu rather than
call a function (the data table's "Copy payment ID" writes to the clipboard), and the column's header cell has a
screen-reader name ("Actions") where shadcn's is empty. See [Actions per row](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md#actions-per-row).

#### Pagination: built from a Spring Data page

The parts are shadcn's (`PaginationContent`, `-Item`, `-Link`, `-Previous`, `-Next`, `-Ellipsis`), and
`<sl:pagination th:page="${people}"/>` with no content renders them all from a Spring Data `Page`: links that keep the
request's other parameters, first and last page, ellipses, Previous and Next disabled at the ends (no `href`,
`aria-disabled`). `isActive` is `active`. The ellipsis is not `aria-hidden`: it reads "More pages", where shadcn's
hidden screen-reader text is never read. The labels are messages (`sl.pagination.*`) rather than props such as
Previous's `text`. The data table's footer pieces are components: `sl:pagination-summary` ("11–20 of 270") and
`sl:pagination-size` (a menu of links rather than a select). See [Pagination](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/pagination.md).

#### Chart: parts with props instead of Recharts JSX

`<sl:chart th:data="${rows}">` is `ChartContainer` with the chart inside it, and its parts are Recharts' components
with shadcn's settings: `sl:chart-grid` (`CartesianGrid vertical={false}`), `sl:chart-x-axis` and `sl:chart-y-axis`
(no tick or axis lines), `sl:chart-tooltip` (`ChartTooltip` with `ChartTooltipContent`), `sl:chart-legend` and the
series, `sl:chart-bar`, `sl:chart-line` and `sl:chart-area`. Their props are Recharts' and shadcn's in kebab case
(`indicator`, `hide-label`, `label-key`, `tick-margin`, `radius`; `stackId` is `stack`, `type` is `curve`, `dot` is
`dots`). The chart type follows the series: there is no `BarChart` to pick. What differs:

- **No `ChartConfig`.** A series' `label` and `color` sit on its part, and `color-dark` replaces the config's
  `theme`, written as `light-dark()`. A series without a colour takes the next `--chart-N`; shadcn's examples name
  them in the config.
- **No `ChartStyle`.** shadcn writes the `--color-<key>` properties into a `<style>` element, which a strict
  Content-Security-Policy blocks: its chart loses its colours. Shadleaf sets them through CSSOM. A key is therefore
  checked to be a CSS identifier.
- **Named formats instead of functions.** `tickFormatter`, `formatter` and `labelFormatter` are `format`,
  `value-format` and `label-format` with a name (`month-short`, `compact`, `currency`), written with `Intl` in the
  page's language. Dates are read by their Java type, not by `new Date()`, so a `LocalDate` never shifts a day.
- **The chart's name is an `aria-label`**, not Recharts' `title`: a browser shows an svg's `<title>` as a native
  tooltip over the styled one. And the tooltip keeps a gap between a series' name and its value, which shadcn's lets
  touch once the tooltip is wider than its minimum.
- **A visible focus ring.** shadcn hides the chart's (`outline-hidden` on `.recharts-surface`); the chart takes the
  focus for its arrow keys, so each skin draws one.
- **Recharts 3.10 on Preact**, not React, and not the 3.8 shadcn pins: the script is smaller, and 3.10 fixes a line
  drawn only partway with reduced motion.
- **Not there yet:** pie, radar and radial charts, horizontal bars, gradients, icons in the tooltip and legend, and
  custom tooltip or legend content.

See [Chart](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/chart.md).

#### Sidebar: one element instead of a Sheet on a phone

shadcn's `Sidebar` renders a `Sheet` on a phone and a separate sidebar on a desktop, chosen in the browser by
`useIsMobile()`. The server does not know the screen's width, and rendering the navigation twice would double its
markup and its ids, so `<sl:sidebar>` is one `<nav popover>`: CSS shows it beside the page from 768 px, and below that
the trigger opens it as the panel (focus in, the rest of the page inert while it is open). The state lives on
`<sl:sidebar-provider>`'s `data-state` (shadcn also puts it on the sidebar), the cookie is `sl-sidebar-state` with
`expanded` or `collapsed` (shadcn's `sidebar_state` holds `true` or `false`) for a year instead of a week, and the
server reads it: `defaultOpen` is `default-state`, `open` is `state`, and there is no `onOpenChange` or `useSidebar()`;
the `sl-sidebar-toggle` event tells a script. `side="right"` and `"left"` are the end and the start of a line, as
for the sheet, and the trigger's icon turns round by itself for a sidebar on the end (shadcn's sidebar-14 adds
`rotate-180`). `variant` is shadcn's (`sidebar`, `floating`, `inset`) and, as there, changes the desktop only.
So does `collapsible`: `offcanvas` and `icon` as shadcn's, while `none` only keeps the sidebar from collapsing on a
desktop and is still the panel on a phone (shadcn's is a plain column at every width). See
[Sidebar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md).

The parts inside it keep shadcn's names. `<sl:sidebar-menu-button>` is a link unless `as="button"` (shadcn's renders a
button, and `asChild` makes it a link); `isActive` is `active`, and `th:active="${#slNav.current('/people')}"` asks the
request whether the link is the current page, so no controller has to say so. The icon goes in the `icon-start` slot
and the text is wrapped for you (shadcn's `<span>` around the label); two lines are two elements, such as `<strong>`
and `<small>`, as there are no utility classes. `<sl:sidebar-content>` is a `div`, as shadcn's: `<sl:sidebar>` is the
`nav`. `tooltip="Home"` on a menu button is shadcn's `tooltip` prop (a string only).

A collapsible group needs no `Collapsible`, `CollapsibleTrigger` and `CollapsibleContent` around the item, its button
and its sub-menu: `<sl:sidebar-menu-item collapsible>` is a `details` element, its menu button becomes the `summary`
(with shadcn's chevron) and `<sl:sidebar-menu-sub>` the content. `defaultOpen` is `open`, usually
`th:open="${#slNav.current('/settings')}"`. `SidebarMenuSubButton`'s `isActive` is `active`, `size` is shadcn's
(`sm`, `md`), and it is a link unless `as="button"`. sidebar-07 leaves its projects out of the strip of icons with
`group-data-[collapsible=icon]:hidden` on the group; here that is `<sl:sidebar-group icon-hidden>`. sidebar-02 wraps
a group in a `Collapsible` with the label as its trigger; here that is `<sl:sidebar-group collapsible>`. sidebar-08
puts the trigger in a `SidebarMenuAction` beside a link; here that is `<sl:sidebar-menu-sub collapsible
aria-label="...">`, whose chevron needs a name of its own (shadcn's says "Toggle"). sidebar-05's plus and minus are the
turning chevron.

A dropdown menu opened from a menu button or a menu action (shadcn's team switcher, version switcher, `NavUser` and
the projects' "More") is `<sl:dropdown-menu-trigger as="sidebar-menu-button">` or `as="sidebar-menu-action"` (see
above). shadcn picks the side in React, `side={isMobile ? "bottom" : "right"}`; here `side="right"` is enough: in the
phone panel (and in the header layout's row) CSS opens a right or left menu below its trigger, lined up with its end.
shadcn's `data-[state=open]:bg-sidebar-accent` on the team switcher is built in: an open trigger has the active look,
and its menu is at least as wide as the trigger (`w-(--radix-dropdown-menu-trigger-width) min-w-56`). The current team
is a checked radio item (shadcn's team switcher marks none, its version switcher draws a check icon). The team
switcher's shortcuts (⌘1, ⌘2) are left out of the [layout](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/collapses-to-icons.md): shadcn shows them, but
nothing handles the keys. A menu action is
24 px, shadcn's 20 px being too small a target once it shows (WCAG 2.2). See
[Sidebar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md#menus-in-the-sidebar).

#### Site header and the header placement

shadcn/ui has no site header component: sidebar-16 and the dashboard write theirs in each block. `<sl:site-header>` is
that header (a `header` row, with an `end` slot for what goes to the end), and serves as the sidebar-07 page header
inside `<sl:sidebar-inset>` too. shadcn/ui's sidebar has no header placement either: `placement="header"` on
`<sl:sidebar>` makes the same element a row of links in the site header from 768 px (Flux's header layout) and the
panel on a phone, and `panel-only` on a header, footer, group or menu item leaves it out of everything but the phone
panel. See [Sidebar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md#in-the-header) and [Site Header](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/site-header.md). sidebar-16's
layout itself (that header across the whole page, the sidebar below it) is not supported: the sidebar is sticky at the
top of the screen, so `<sl:sidebar-provider>` has to start at the top of the page. The Layouts section has the
layouts there are, from [Sub-menus](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/sub-menus.md) on.

#### User menu: a component, not a block

shadcn's `NavUser` is part of its sidebar blocks, with the user passed in as props and a Log out item that does
nothing. `<sl:user-menu>` is a component: the user comes from Spring Security (`#slUser`), Sign out posts a form with
the CSRF token, and an anonymous visitor gets a Sign in link. `placement="header"` gives the picture-only button for a site
header. The avatar stays round in the menu, where `NavUser` makes it a rounded square, and the menu's items are what you
put inside the component (shadcn's "Upgrade to Pro", "Account", "Billing" and "Notifications" are the block's own). The
team switcher and the version switcher stay examples on the Sidebar page, as in shadcn's docs: see
[Menus in the sidebar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md#menus-in-the-sidebar).

#### Breadcrumb: the ellipsis opens its own menu

The parts are shadcn's (`BreadcrumbList`, `-Item`, `-Link`, `-Page`, `-Separator`, `-Ellipsis`). `<sl:breadcrumb-link>`
is always a link (shadcn's `asChild` makes it a router `Link`); a level without a page is plain text in its item.
shadcn's example wraps the ellipsis in a `DropdownMenuTrigger` by hand; here `<sl:breadcrumb-ellipsis>` with
`sl:dropdown-menu-item`s as its content renders that menu and its button itself. The ellipsis's hidden text is
"More levels", not "More", and the separator turns around on a right-to-left page. See
[Breadcrumb](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/breadcrumb.md).

#### Attachment: a trigger with `as`, and a label for the group

The parts and props are shadcn's. `<AttachmentTrigger asChild>` around a link is `<sl:attachment-trigger as="a">`, and
inside a `DialogTrigger` it is a trigger with `commandfor` and `command="show-modal"`. `<sl:attachment-action>`
takes `as="a"` too, for a download link. Where shadcn tells you to add `tabIndex`, `role="group"` and an `aria-label`
to a group of attachments without actions, `<sl:attachment-group label="...">` adds all three. shadcn's `shimmer` and
`scroll-fade-x` utilities are part of the attachment's stylesheet. See [Attachment](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/attachment.md).

#### Skip link and main

shadcn/ui has no skip link; `<sl:skip-link>` goes first in the body and skips to `<sl:sidebar-inset>`, which therefore
renders `id="main"` and `tabindex="-1"` (shadcn's `SidebarInset` is a bare `main`). See
[Skip Link](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/skip-link.md).

#### Markup

The rendered markup uses class names (`class="card-header"`) where shadcn uses `data-slot="card-header"`, and a
`data-variant` or `data-size` attribute only when the value is not the default. It matters only if you port CSS written
against shadcn's markup.

### Deliberate differences

#### A button does not submit by default

`<sl:button>` renders `type="button"`; shadcn's `Button` leaves the type out, so it submits the form it is in. Write
`type="submit"` on the button that should submit. See [Button](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/button.md).

#### An alert is not announced by default

shadcn's `Alert` always has `role="alert"`, so a screen reader interrupts the user to read it. Most alerts are part of
the page when it loads, where that interruption helps nobody. Add `role="alert"` yourself when an alert appears later,
for example in an htmx response. See [Alert](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/alert.md).

#### Contrast

A few of shadcn's colour pairs are under the 4.5:1 contrast WCAG asks for small text:

- destructive text on its light red tint (the destructive button and badge, the destructive alert);
- muted text on a muted background (the kbd, the avatar's initials).

Shadleaf mixes 20% of `--foreground` into the text colour in those places. It still follows your own `--destructive`
and `--muted-foreground`, so your theme keeps working.

Where shadcn changes text to `--muted-foreground` on hover, Shadleaf keeps `--foreground`, for the same reason.

#### Only interactive elements react to hover

shadcn's ghost badge changes colour on hover even when it is a plain label. A Shadleaf badge only reacts to hover, and
takes keyboard focus, when it is a link (`as="a"`).

#### Accessibility additions

- `<sl:card-title level="3">` is announced as a heading, so screen reader users can jump between cards. Without a
  `level` it is plain text, as in shadcn. The same goes for `<sl:empty-title>`.
- The avatar is hidden from assistive technology unless it has a `label`, as it usually sits next to the person's
  name. With one, it is announced as a single image with that name.
- The skeleton is hidden from assistive technology; put `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading.
- A tab panel shows the focus ring when Tab reaches it; shadcn's takes the focus without showing it. In Windows'
  high-contrast mode the active tab is underlined, as its background and shadow are gone there.
- The attachment trigger draws the skin's focus ring around the card, only for keyboard focus; shadcn's card shows a
  faint ring whenever anything in it has focus, a click included. An uploading or processing attachment is marked
  `aria-busy`, and its title does not shimmer for users who ask for reduced motion or in Windows' high-contrast mode.
  A failed attachment's text uses the legible destructive colour (see Contrast). The edges of an attachment group
  stop fading while it has keyboard focus, so its focus ring shows.
- Rendering fails when a component that needs an accessible name has none, such as an icon-only button without an
  `aria-label`.

#### Menus and tooltips

- Keyboard focus on a menu item draws the focus ring as well as the accent background, which alone is barely lighter
  than the menu. The pointer highlights with the background only, as in shadcn.
- Tab closes a menu and moves on to the next control, as the ARIA menu pattern describes; Radix keeps the focus in
  the menu.
- A tooltip waits 300 ms before it shows on hover (`delay`), where shadcn shows it at once, so moving the pointer
  across a toolbar does not flash every tooltip on the way. Keyboard focus, and the next tooltip right after one hid,
  still show at once.
- The pointer can move onto a tooltip without it hiding, and Escape hides it, as WCAG 1.4.13 asks.
- `mode="label"` is for a tooltip that repeats its trigger's name, such as an icon button's `aria-label`: it is hidden
  from screen readers instead of describing the trigger with the same words. shadcn has no such option.

#### Toasts

- A toast shows for 5 seconds, not Sonner's 4, and its time stops while it has the focus as well as on hover. Every
  toast has a close button (Sonner's `closeButton` is off by default), and there is no swipe to dismiss.
- There is no action or cancel button: a toast goes away by itself, so it must not hold the only way to do something.
- An error toast is announced at once (assertive); the others politely, as all of Sonner's are.
- An error's icon takes the destructive colour; with Sonner every icon has the text colour unless `richColors` is on.
- The toasts move into an open modal dialog, so one shown while a dialog is open can be used and is announced; a
  Sonner toast outside the dialog is inert there.

#### Breadcrumb

- The page shown now is plain text with `aria-current="page"`. shadcn's also has `role="link"` and
  `aria-disabled="true"`, which a screen reader announces as a link that goes nowhere.
- An ellipsis without a menu is read as "More levels"; shadcn's is hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`) even
  though it holds a visually hidden "More".
- The ellipsis's menu button is named "Show more levels" rather than shadcn's example's "Toggle menu".

#### Sidebar menus

- A group with a label is a group named by it (`role="group"`, `aria-labelledby`), so a screen reader says "Platform,
  group" when the focus moves into it; shadcn's label is plain text.
- The current page's menu button has `aria-current="page"` (`aria-current="true"` for a button), which a screen reader
  says; shadcn sets only `data-active`. The skins style `aria-current`, and in Windows' high-contrast mode the current
  entry keeps an outline, as its background is gone there.
- A menu badge describes its button (`aria-describedby`), so a screen reader says "Inbox, link, 12 unread" when Tab
  reaches the link; shadcn's badge is only read when reading through the list. `label` gives the words to say.
- The group and menu actions need an `aria-label` (shadcn's examples put a visually hidden `<span>` in them). A menu
  action is 24 px at every width, and a group action on a phone, WCAG 2.2's minimum target size, instead of 20 px with
  a larger invisible hit area.
- Collapsed to icons, a menu button's tooltip and its dropdown menu are never shown together.
- `show-on-hover` is `showOnHover`.
- Collapsed to icons, a menu button's tooltip repeats its name, so it is hidden from screen readers and describes
  nothing (`sl:tooltip`'s `mode="label"`); Radix's tooltip makes it the button's description, which a screen reader
  says after the same name. The tooltip shows on keyboard focus too, after the delay on hover.
- Collapsed to icons, a click on a collapsible group's icon expands the sidebar and opens the group; shadcn's opens the
  group, whose sub-menu the strip hides. A group that holds the current page shows it on its icon, which shadcn's does
  not. A collapsible item takes no badge or action (the browser hides them with the sub-menu).

#### Form controls

- `<sl:input>` only takes the text-like types (`text`, `email`, `password`, `date`, `file`, ...). Checkboxes, radio
  buttons and switches are separate components, as in shadcn, but shadcn's `Input` would accept `type="checkbox"`.
- `<sl:native-select>` takes `<option>` and `<optgroup>` as they are; there is no `NativeSelectOption`.
- The select's list is at least as wide as the select and opens below it, where shadcn's default
  (`position="item-aligned"`) lays it over the select. Keyboard focus on an item draws the focus ring as well as the
  accent background, as in the dropdown menu.
- Checkbox, radio group and switch are the browser's own inputs, styled, where shadcn builds them from buttons. They
  submit with the form without a hidden input of their own, `th:field` binds them, and the keyboard works as it does
  on any radio button or checkbox. The indeterminate state is the input's own (`indeterminate` prop, or the DOM
  property) and shows a minus; shadcn's checkbox shows its check mark for `checked="indeterminate"`.
- Input group: `className="border-b"` (or `border-t`) on a block addon is its `border` prop, and the `ml-auto` of
  shadcn's examples is not needed: in an addon above or below the control, `<sl:input-group-text>` takes the free
  space. A disabled control fades the whole group by itself, where shadcn's needs `data-disabled` on the group. Only
  `<sl:input-group-input>` and `<sl:input-group-textarea>` are controls: there is no `data-slot="input-group-control"`
  for a control of your own. A click on an addon focuses the control only with JavaScript.
- A disabled checkbox fades as a whole, check mark included. In the lyra and nova skins a disabled native select and
  select get the same grey background as a disabled input (shadcn's lyra and nova only give it to input and textarea).

#### Field

- `th:field` goes on `<sl:field>` (or `<sl:field-set>`), which wires up the label's `for`, the control's `id`,
  `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`, and the field's `data-invalid`. In shadcn you set `htmlFor`, `id`,
  `aria-invalid` and `data-invalid` yourself.
- `<sl:field-error/>` reads the binding's messages; there is no `errors` prop. Content of your own replaces them, as
  `children` do in shadcn.
- The error has no `role="alert"`: after a full page load every error would be announced at once. The control is
  described by its error instead.
- The field has no `role="group"`, which gave every field an unnamed group. A set of options is a `<sl:field-set>`.
- In an invalid field, only the label (or legend) and the error turn destructive; shadcn colours all the field's
  text.
- No `FieldTitle`, `FieldSeparator` or choice cards (a field inside a label) yet.
- No `data-disabled` on the field: its label fades by itself when the control is disabled, also by a
  `<sl:field-set disabled>`. The description does not fade.

#### Additions

- An input, textarea or native select with `th:field` marks itself `aria-invalid` when its field has errors, so the
  invalid style needs no markup of yours.
- `<sl:form-errors/>` shows the binding's global errors (`reject(...)`, a class-level constraint), or with
  `show="all"` every error, as a destructive alert above the fields. shadcn has no such component; you would write an `Alert` with the messages yourself.
- A read-only input or textarea gets a muted background and no shadow; shadcn draws it as an editable one.
- In Windows' high-contrast mode a disabled control turns the system's grey text colour (`GrayText`) instead of
  fading.
- `<sl:button loading>` shows a spinner, disables the button and announces the busy state. In shadcn you put a
  `Spinner` in the button and disable it yourself.
- `<sl:spinner>` turns slower, not still, when the user asks for reduced motion; shadcn's keeps spinning at full
  speed. Its name, "Loading", is a message (`sl.spinner.label`) you can translate.

---

## IDE completion

> Completion for sl:* tags, their attributes and values in IntelliJ IDEA and WebStorm.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/ide-completion/

IntelliJ IDEA and WebStorm complete `<sl:button>`, its attributes and their allowed values from a
[web-types](https://github.com/JetBrains/web-types) file. The IDE finds that file through the `web-types` property of a
`package.json`, and nowhere else: not inside a jar, not from a URL. The file does not need Node.js to be installed.

### Let your application write it

Set this property for development, for example in `application-local.properties`:

```properties
shadleaf.dev.web-types-file=shadleaf.web-types.json
```

When the application starts, it writes the file from its own component registry, relative to the working directory
(the project root, when you run it from the IDE or with `mvn spring-boot:run`). That makes it exact for your
application: a template you copied into your project and changed, and components of your own under
`templates/sl/components/`, are in it too. It is only rewritten when something changed.

Then reference it from a `package.json` in the project root. A Maven-only project needs nothing more than this:

```json
{
  "name": "my-application",
  "private": true,
  "web-types": "./shadleaf.web-types.json"
}
```

Add `shadleaf.web-types.json` to `.gitignore`, and commit the `package.json`. If the project already has a
`package.json`, add the `web-types` property to it; it also takes an array of paths.

### Or download it

The file for this version of the docs, describing the library's own components:
[shadleaf.web-types.json](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/shadleaf.web-types.json). Save it next to the
`package.json` above.

### What it contains

For every component, the props its template declares: an enum's `values`, the `default`, a `boolean` prop as an
attribute without a value, and the prop's description. Each prop is offered a second time as `th:<prop>`, for a value
from an expression. The attribute tables in these docs are generated from the same data.

---

## Using Shadleaf with coding agents

> Point Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and other coding agents at these docs, and give them the rules they get wrong.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/coding-agents/

Coding agents are great company when you build with Shadleaf, with a little help to get started. Shadleaf is new, so
models haven't learned it yet, and because it looks so much like shadcn/ui, an agent tends to reach for what it knows
from React: a `<Button asChild>`, a few Tailwind classes, or a `<sl:dialog-trigger>` that doesn't exist.

The good news is that two small steps take care of most of this: a few rules in the file your agent reads at the start
of every session, and docs it can read as Markdown. Both take only a couple of minutes to set up.

### Add the rules to your project

Paste this into the instructions file your agent reads: `AGENTS.md` (Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI and most
others), `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code) or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. Replace `<version>` with the Shadleaf version in
your `pom.xml`, so the agent reads the docs of the version you use.

```markdown
## Shadleaf (Thymeleaf UI components)

- The UI uses Shadleaf: shadcn/ui as Thymeleaf tags with the `sl:` prefix
  (`xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"`), rendered on the server. Not React: no JSX, no Radix, no `asChild`.
- Docs as Markdown: https://shadleaf.dev/<version>/llms.txt. Read the component's page
  (`.../components/<name>.md`) before using a component; it ends with the attribute table.
- An attribute that is not a prop passes through to the HTML silently, so a misspelt prop does nothing.
  Use only the props in the attribute table; `th:<prop>="${...}"` sets one from an expression.
- Change a component's look with its props (`variant`, `size`, `border`, ...), not with utility classes:
  the library's stylesheet defines none. `class` is appended to the component's own class.
- A link that looks like a button is `<sl:button as="a" th:href="@{/x}">`. `<sl:button>` renders
  `type="button"`: write `type="submit"` on the one that submits a form.
- Forms: `th:object` on the `<form>`, `th:field` on `<sl:field>` (its label, control and errors share it),
  `<sl:form-errors/>` before the fields.
- Dialogs and sheets need an `id` and open from any button with `commandfor="<id>" command="show-modal"`
  (`command="close"` closes). There are no trigger or close parts. Menus and popovers open with
  `<sl:dropdown-menu-trigger>` / `<sl:popover-trigger>` or `popovertarget`.
- Icons: `<sl:icon name="...">` with Lucide names. An icon-only button (`size="icon"`, `icon-sm`, ...)
  needs an `aria-label`; rendering fails without one.
- Charts: `<sl:chart th:data="${rows}" label="...">` with parts (`sl:chart-x-axis key="month"`,
  `sl:chart-bar key="desktop" th:label="#{...}"`). No `ChartConfig` and no formatter functions: labels and
  colours go on the series parts, number and date formats are names (`format="month-short"`).
- Rendering fails with a message on a wrong prop value, a missing required prop or a missing accessible
  name: render every page you change (run the tests or load the page) and fix what it reports.
- With `hx-boost` on `<body>`, every boosted page load sends `HX-Request`: return a fragment only when the
  request targets one (see the "Application shell" guide, "With htmx").
```

Then tell the agent how your application loads Shadleaf's CSS and Alpine.js, as that changes what it may write. Add
the line for each setting that matches your `application.properties`, below the others:

```markdown
<!-- shadleaf.assets.variant: keep one -->
- CSS: `standalone` (the default). The application does not compile Tailwind, so utility classes do nothing;
  style the application's own markup in its own stylesheet.
- CSS: `embedded`. The application compiles Tailwind; utility classes work for layout, also in `class` on a
  component, but never to restyle one.

<!-- shadleaf.assets.alpine: keep one -->
- Alpine: `bundled` (the default). Shadleaf loads and starts Alpine.js; never add another Alpine script.
  Register the application's own `Alpine.data` on `alpine:init`, in a script before the `sl/layout :: assets`
  fragment.
- Alpine: `csp`. As `bundled`, with Alpine's CSP build: no arrow functions, template literals, spread,
  nested assignments or globals (`Math`, `document`) in `x-*` attributes; put that logic in `Alpine.data`.
- Alpine: `external`. The application loads Alpine.js itself; its script goes after the
  `sl/layout :: assets` fragment, and it registers the Alpine plugins it needs.
```

See the [Tailwind CSS guide](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tailwind.md) and the [Alpine.js guide](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/alpine.md) for
what each setting does.

Keep it short: it is loaded in every session. Your coding agent will read more documentation as it needs.

### Docs as Markdown

Every page of these docs has a Markdown copy at the same address with `.md` instead of the trailing slash:
`components/button/` is `components/button.md`. The examples in it are the Thymeleaf source, and the attribute table is
a Markdown table, so an agent gets what you see here without parsing HTML.

The site's root also has the files of the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) convention:

| File                  | Holds                                                                                       |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `llms.txt`            | Every page with a one-line description, linking the Markdown copies. Start an agent here.   |
| `llms-full.txt`       | All pages in one file. Large; most agents do better with the index and the pages they need. |
| `llms-components.txt` | All component pages in one file: every example and attribute table.                         |
| `llms-guides.txt`     | The "Start here" pages, the layouts and the guides in one file.                             |

Every version of the docs has its own set, under `/<version>/`; `/current/` is the latest release.
In a session without the rules above, a prompt such as "read https://shadleaf.dev/current/llms.txt,
then add a delete confirmation to the members table" is enough to get started.

---

## Components

> Every Shadleaf component, in the groups of the sidebar, with one line on what each is for.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/

Every component is a Thymeleaf tag with the `sl:` prefix, rendered on the server. Each page shows examples, the
markup to write, and a table of the component's attributes. Whole pages built from them are in
[Layouts](../layouts/.

### Actions

- [Button](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/button.md): A button, or a link that looks like one.
- [Theme Toggle](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/theme-toggle.md): Switches the page between the light and the dark theme, and remembers the choice in the browser.

### Forms

- [Field](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/field.md): A label, a control, a description and the binding's error messages, wired together from one th:field.
- [Form errors](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/form-errors.md): The errors that belong to the whole form rather than one field, or all of the form's errors, read from the binding and shown above the fields.
- [Label](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/label.md): A label for a form control.
- [Input](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/input.md): A text input, bound to a form field with th:field.
- [Input Group](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/input-group.md): Text, icons and buttons inside the border of an input or textarea.
- [Textarea](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/textarea.md): A multi-line text input, bound to a form field with th:field.
- [Select](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/select.md): shadcn/ui's Select on a real select element, bound with th:field; the browser's customizable select where it has one.
- [Select (Native)](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/select-native.md): The browser's own select, styled, bound to a form field with th:field.
- [Combobox](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/combobox.md): shadcn/ui's Combobox on a real select element, bound with th:field; type to filter, choose one value or several as chips, and load the options from the server as you type.
- [Checkbox](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/checkbox.md): The browser's own checkbox, styled, bound to a form field with th:field.
- [Radio Group](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/radio-group.md): A set of the browser's own radio buttons, styled, bound to a form field with th:field.
- [Switch](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/switch.md): An on/off control, bound to a boolean form field with th:field.
- [Toggle](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/toggle.md): A button that is on or off, as a checkbox drawn as a button, bound to a boolean form field with th:field.
- [Toggle Group](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/toggle-group.md): A set of toggles of which one or several can be on, as radio buttons or checkboxes bound with th:field.
- [Calendar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/calendar.md): shadcn/ui's Calendar over native date inputs, bound with th:field; a date or a range of dates.
- [Date Picker](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/date-picker.md): A button showing the chosen date that opens a calendar in a popover; a date or a range, bound with th:field.

### Overlays

- [Dialog](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/dialog.md): A modal window over the page, on the native dialog element.
- [Alert Dialog](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/alert-dialog.md): A modal dialog that interrupts the user with something important and waits for an answer.
- [Sheet](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sheet.md): A dialog that slides in from an edge of the screen.
- [Popover](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/popover.md): Rich content in a panel next to the button that opens it, on the browser's Popover API.
- [Dropdown Menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/dropdown-menu.md): A menu of actions or links that opens from a button, on the browser's Popover API.
- [Tooltip](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/tooltip.md): A short text that shows while the pointer rests on an element or the keyboard focuses it.

### Feedback

- [Alert](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/alert.md): A callout for a message the user should notice.
- [Toast](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/toast.md): A short message in a corner of the page that closes itself, sent by the server; shadcn/ui's Sonner.
- [Skeleton](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/skeleton.md): A placeholder that pulses while content loads.
- [Spinner](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/spinner.md): A spinning icon that says something is loading.
- [Empty](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/empty.md): What a list, a table, a search or a page shows when there is nothing to show yet.

### Data

- [Table](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md): A table in shadcn/ui's look, whose column headers sort it on the server.
- [Pagination](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/pagination.md): Links to the other pages of a list, built from the Spring Data Page the controller returns.
- [Query params](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/query-params.md): Hidden inputs that keep a table's order, page size and filters when a search form is sent.
- [Month view](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/month-view.md): A month rendered on the server, with content of your own per day and a link per day; no picking.
- [Chart](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/chart.md): shadcn/ui's Chart, Recharts drawing bars, lines and areas from rows the controller puts in the model; labels and colours on the series, named Intl formats.

### Application shell

Start with the [overview](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md): Choosing between a sidebar and a header for the frame around every page, and what every layout needs whichever you pick.

- [Sidebar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md): The application's navigation beside the page, and a panel over it on a phone.
- [Site Header](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/site-header.md): A header bar across the top of the page, or at the top of the sidebar layout's page.
- [User Menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/user-menu.md): The signed-in user with a menu that signs out, or a Sign in link, for the sidebar's footer or the site header.
- [Breadcrumb](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/breadcrumb.md): The trail of pages above the one shown now, with a menu for the levels a long trail leaves out.
- [Skip Link](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/skip-link.md): A link past the navigation to the page's content, for keyboard users.

### Disclosure

- [Tabs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/tabs.md): Panels of content shown one at a time, chosen from a row of tabs.
- [Accordion](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/accordion.md): A stack of sections, each with a heading that shows or hides its content, on the browser's details element.
- [Collapsible](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/collapsible.md): Content that a button shows and hides, on the browser's details element.

### Display

- [Card](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/card.md): A container for related content and actions, built from its parts.
- [Attachment](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/attachment.md): A file or an image attached to a message, a form or a record, with its name, its size or state, and actions.
- [Badge](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/badge.md): A small label for a status, a count or a category.
- [Avatar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/avatar.md): A picture of a person, with initials when there is no picture.
- [Icon](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/icon.md): Inline SVG icons from lucide, or your own.
- [Kbd](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/kbd.md): A key on the keyboard, or a combination of keys.
- [Separator](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/separator.md): A thin line between content.

---

## Button

> A button, or a link that looks like one.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/button/

**Example: Button.**

```html
<sl:button>Save</sl:button>
```

### A button never submits by accident

`<sl:button>` renders `type="button"`, not HTML's default `submit`. A button inside a form therefore does nothing
unless you say so: write `type="submit"` on the one that should submit.

**Example: In a form.** Only the button that says type="submit" submits the form.

```html
<form method="post" th:action="@{/orders}">
  <sl:button type="submit">Save</sl:button>
  <sl:button variant="outline">Preview</sl:button>
</form>
```

### Variants

**Example: Variants.**

```html
<sl:button>Default</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="outline">Outline</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="ghost">Ghost</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="destructive">Destructive</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="secondary">Secondary</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="link">Link</sl:button>
```

### Sizes

**Example: Sizes.**

```html
<sl:button size="xs">Extra small</sl:button>
<sl:button size="sm">Small</sl:button>
<sl:button>Default</sl:button>
<sl:button size="lg">Large</sl:button>
```

The `icon` sizes are square, for a button holding only an icon. Such a button has no text for a screen reader, so it
must have an `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`); rendering fails without one.

**Example: Icon-only sizes.** An icon-only button needs an aria-label; rendering fails without one.

```html
<sl:button size="icon-xs" variant="outline" aria-label="Add"><sl:icon name="plus"/></sl:button>
<sl:button size="icon-sm" variant="outline" aria-label="Add"><sl:icon name="plus"/></sl:button>
<sl:button size="icon" variant="outline" aria-label="Add"><sl:icon name="plus"/></sl:button>
<sl:button size="icon-lg" variant="outline" aria-label="Add"><sl:icon name="plus"/></sl:button>
```

### With an icon

Put an [`<sl:icon>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/icon.md) in the `icon-start` or `icon-end` slot. It takes the button's colour and a 16 pixel size.

**Example: With an icon.**

```html
<sl:button variant="destructive">
  <sl:slot name="icon-start"><sl:icon name="trash"/></sl:slot>
  Delete order
</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="outline">
  Next
  <sl:slot name="icon-end"><sl:icon name="arrow-right"/></sl:slot>
</sl:button>
```

### As a link

`as="a"` renders an anchor that looks the same, for navigation.

**Example: As a link.**

```html
<sl:button as="a" href="/orders" variant="outline">View orders</sl:button>
<sl:button as="a" href="/orders" variant="link">View orders</sl:button>
```

### Disabled and loading

A disabled button gets the native `disabled` attribute. A disabled link loses its `href`, leaves the tab order and is
marked `aria-disabled`, so it cannot be followed. `loading` shows a spinner in place of the start icon, announces the
busy state with `aria-busy` and a visually hidden "Loading" label, and disables the button.

**Example: Disabled.**

```html
<sl:button disabled>Save</sl:button>
<sl:button as="a" href="/orders" variant="outline" disabled>View orders</sl:button>
```
**Example: Loading.**

```html
<sl:button loading>Saving</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="outline" loading>
  <sl:slot name="icon-start"><sl:icon name="save"/></sl:slot>
  Save
</sl:button>
<sl:button size="icon" variant="outline" aria-label="Refresh" loading><sl:icon name="refresh-cw"/></sl:button>
```

The "Loading" label comes from the message `sl.button.loading`; define it in your own `messages.properties` to
translate or reword it.

### Props from expressions

Every prop also has a `th:` form that takes a Thymeleaf expression.

**Example: Props from an expression.**

```html
<sl:button th:variant="${order.cancellable ? 'destructive' : 'secondary'}"
           th:text="#{orders.cancel}">Cancel order</sl:button>
```

### Everything else passes through

Attributes that are not props, such as `hx-*`, `x-*`, `aria-*` and `data-*`, land on the rendered element unchanged,
so the button works with htmx and Alpine. `class` is appended to the component's own class.

**Example: Pass-through attributes.** Anything that is not a prop lands on the rendered element; class is appended.

```html
<sl:button variant="outline" class="app-wide"
           hx-post="/orders/42/archive" hx-target="#orders"
           data-testid="archive">Archive</sl:button>
```

### Attributes

Attributes of `<sl:button>`: A button, or with `as="a"` an anchor that looks the same. Every attribute that is not a prop (`hx-*`, `x-*`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `href`) passes through; `class` is appended to `button`.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `default`, `outline`, `ghost`, `destructive`, `secondary`, `link` | `default` | Visual style of the button. |
| `size` | `xs`, `sm`, `default`, `lg`, `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`, `icon-lg` | `default` | Size of the button. The `icon` sizes are square, for a button that holds only an icon, and need an `aria-label`. |
| `as` | `button`, `a` | `button` | Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`) for navigation. |
| `type` | `button`, `submit`, `reset` | `button` | Submit behaviour. Defaults to `button`, unlike HTML, so a button in a form never submits by accident. |
| `disabled` | *boolean* | — | Disable the button. A disabled anchor loses its `href` and leaves the tab order. |
| `loading` | *boolean* | — | Show a spinner, announce the busy state and disable the button. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:variant="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is required when `size` is `icon` or `icon-xs` or `icon-sm` or `icon-lg`; rendering fails without one.

---

## Theme Toggle

> Switches the page between the light and the dark theme, and remembers the choice in the browser.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/theme-toggle/

**Example: Theme toggle.** An icon button opening a menu with Light, Dark and System; the icon shows the page's theme.

```html
<sl:theme-toggle/>
```

### Usage

Put the theme script in the `<head>` of your layout, as [Getting started](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/getting-started.md) shows, and the
toggle wherever it belongs, usually the page header:

```html
<head>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: theme-script}"></th:block>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: assets}"></th:block>
</head>
<body>
<header>
  ...
  <sl:theme-toggle/>
</header>
```

The toggle is an icon button that opens a menu with **Light**, **Dark** and **System**. Light and Dark are stored in
the browser (`localStorage`, key `shadleaf-theme`); System removes the key, and the page follows the operating system
again. The theme script reads that key before the first paint, so every page after the choice starts in the right
theme, with no flash of the other one.

The button shows a sun in the light theme and a moon in the dark one. A screen reader hears something like "Theme, menu
button"; in the menu, "Light, checked, menu item radio, 1 of 3" (the wording differs between screen readers).

### One button

`as="button"` makes it one button that switches between light and dark. It is a toggle button for dark mode: a screen
reader hears "Dark mode, toggle button, pressed" while the page is dark.

**Example: One button.** as="button" switches between light and dark with one press (aria-pressed is on while dark).

```html
<sl:theme-toggle as="button" variant="ghost"/>
```

Pressing it stores light or dark, so once pressed the page no longer follows the operating system. Use the menu where
that matters.

### What the server renders

The server cannot know what the browser stored, so neither the menu's check mark nor the button's pressed state is in
the markup: the toggle's Alpine component sets them when it starts. Nothing shows wrong in the meantime. The icon comes
from the `dark` class the theme script put on `<html>` before the first paint, and the menu is closed until someone
opens it. A toggle that htmx swaps in, or brings back from its history cache, works the same way.

### Several toggles, several tabs

Every toggle on the page shows the same state, and a choice made in another tab of the same site changes this page
too. While the choice is System, the page follows the operating system when it switches between light and dark (at
sunset, say). Each toggle on a page needs its own `id` when it is a menu:

```html
<sl:theme-toggle id="header-theme" variant="ghost"/>
...
<sl:theme-toggle id="footer-theme" side="top"/>
```

### Labels

The labels are messages, which your `messages.properties` can reword or translate:

```properties
sl.theme-toggle.label=Theme
sl.theme-toggle.dark-mode=Dark mode
sl.theme-toggle.light=Light
sl.theme-toggle.dark=Dark
sl.theme-toggle.system=System
```

`sl.theme-toggle.label` names the menu's button and `sl.theme-toggle.dark-mode` the single button; an `aria-label` on
`<sl:theme-toggle>` replaces either for one toggle.

There is no tooltip. The sun and the moon are what people look for, and a [tooltip](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/tooltip.md) would only repeat the
button's name to a screen reader, as its description.

### Without JavaScript

Nothing can store a choice without JavaScript, and the theme script cannot run either, so the page stays light. The
toggle is then not shown at all (`@media (scripting: none)`), rather than shown and doing nothing.

### Left out

- **More themes than light and dark.** The theme script and the skins know the `dark` class only.
- **A choice stored on the server** (a user setting). Render `class="dark"` on `<html>` yourself and leave out the
  theme script and the toggle; the toggle stores in the browser only.
- **The keyboard shortcut** shadcn's own site has (D). Your application can add one that clicks the toggle.

### Attributes

Attributes of `<sl:theme-toggle>`: Switches the page between the light and the dark theme, and remembers the choice in the browser under the key the theme script (`sl/layout :: theme-script`) reads before the first paint, so the next page starts in it. By default an icon button opening a menu with Light, Dark and System; with `as="button"` one button that switches between light and dark. Its icon shows the theme the page is in. Needs Alpine; without JavaScript it is not shown. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through to the button.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `menu`, `button` | `menu` | `menu`: a menu with Light, Dark and System (`menuitemradio`s). `button`: one toggle button for dark mode (`aria-pressed`), which cannot go back to following the system. |
| `id` | *string* | `theme-toggle` | The menu's id (its button gets the id with `-trigger` added). Two menus on a page need different ids. With `as="button"` it is the button's id, rendered only when set. |
| `variant` | `default`, `outline`, `ghost`, `destructive`, `secondary`, `link` | `outline` | Visual style of the button, as on `sl:button`. |
