read out because of the focus, and needs no role; see [Forms with htmx](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/htmx.md).

**Example: Announced.** role="alert" makes a screen reader read the alert as soon as it appears.

```html
<sl:alert variant="destructive" role="alert">
  <sl:icon name="circle-alert"/>
  <sl:alert-title>The order could not be saved</sl:alert-title>
  <sl:alert-description>Someone else changed it. Reload the page to see their changes.</sl:alert-description>
</sl:alert>
```

For a message that is not urgent, `role="status"` is announced when the user is idle instead of at once.

### Attributes

#### sl:alert

Attributes of `<sl:alert>`: A callout for a message the user should notice: an optional `sl:icon`, then `sl:alert-title` and `sl:alert-description`. It is not announced by itself; add `role="alert"` when it appears after the page loaded, such as in an htmx response.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `default`, `destructive` | `default` | Visual style of the alert. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:variant="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:alert-title

Attributes of `<sl:alert-title>`: The title of an alert, inside `sl:alert`.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6` | — | Heading level. With it the title is a heading (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`) that screen reader users can jump to; without it, plain text, as in shadcn/ui. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:level="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:alert-description

Attributes of `<sl:alert-description>`: The body of an alert, inside `sl:alert`: text, paragraphs or a list.

`sl:alert-description` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

---

## Toast

> A short message in a corner of the page that closes itself, sent by the server; shadcn/ui's Sonner.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/toast/

**Example: Toast.** The button sends an sl-toast event; the toaster shows it, and a screen reader announces it.

```html
<sl:button variant="outline" x-data
           x-on:click="$dispatch('sl-toast', {title: 'Event has been created', description: 'Monday, January 3rd at 6:00pm'})">
  Show toast
</sl:button>

<sl:toaster id="toaster-default"/>
```

### One toaster, toasts from the server

A toast says what just happened, such as "Member deleted", and goes away by itself. shadcn/ui uses
[Sonner](https://sonner.emilkowal.ski/) for it, with a `<Toaster />` in the layout and `toast("...")` calls in the
browser. In Shadleaf the layout has one `<sl:toaster>`, and the toasts come from the server, in one of three ways:

| Where the message comes from | How it gets to the toaster |
| --- | --- |
| An htmx request | The response header `HX-Trigger` sends the `sl-toast` event with the toast as its detail. |
| A full page load, e.g. after a redirect | The page renders `<sl:toast>`s in the toaster, from a flash attribute. |
| An htmx response that renders markup anyway | An out-of-band swap puts `<sl:toast>`s into the toaster. |

Put the toaster at the end of the layout's `<body>`, and let it render the toasts of a flash attribute:

```html
<body>
  ...
  <sl:toaster>
    <sl:toast th:each="toast : ${toasts}" th:title="${toast.title}" th:description="${toast.description}"
              th:variant="${toast.variant}" th:duration="${toast.duration}"/>
  </sl:toaster>
</body>
```

`Toast` (`io.github.wimdeblauwe.shadleaf.toast.Toast`) is what a controller writes for either path: a title, an
optional description, a variant and an optional duration.

```java
Toast.success("Member deleted")
Toast.error("Could not reach the mail server").withDescription("Your message was saved as a draft.")
Toast.of("Copied").withDuration(Duration.ofSeconds(2))
Toast.warning("Your session ends in 5 minutes").untilClosed()
```

#### From an htmx response: `HX-Trigger`

This is what the toast is for: a controller answering an htmx request says what happened, whatever the response
swaps. With [htmx-spring-boot](https://github.com/wimdeblauwe/htmx-spring-boot):

```java
@HxRequest
@DeleteMapping("/members/{id}")
public String delete(@PathVariable long id, HtmxResponse htmxResponse, Model model) {
  Member member = memberService.delete(id);
  htmxResponse.addTrigger("sl-toast", Toast.success("%s was deleted".formatted(member.name())));
  return "members :: deleted";
}
```

The response gets `HX-Trigger: {"sl-toast": {"title": "Ada Lovelace was deleted", "description": null,
"variant": "success", "duration": null}}`; htmx dispatches the event when the response arrives, and the toaster shows
it. Several toasts in one response are a list: `htmxResponse.addTrigger("sl-toast", List.of(first, second))`.

- **The text is only ever text.** The toaster puts the title and description in with `textContent`, so a name such as
  `<b>Ada</b>` shows as typed and can never inject markup.
- **Use `HX-Trigger`**, not `HX-Trigger-After-Swap` or `-After-Settle`: those are dispatched on the element that sent
  the request, and when the swap removed it (a deleted row), the event reaches no one.
- **Not with a redirect.** An `HX-Redirect` or `HX-Location` loads another page, and the toast with it is gone. Put
  it in a flash attribute instead (next section).

#### After a redirect: a flash attribute

A plain form post that redirects (post/redirect/get) puts the toast in a flash attribute, which the toaster in the
layout renders on the page the redirect loads:

```java
@PostMapping("/contact")
public String send(@Valid ContactForm form, BindingResult bindingResult, RedirectAttributes redirectAttributes) {
  if (bindingResult.hasErrors()) {
    return "contact";
  }
  contactService.send(form);
  redirectAttributes.addFlashAttribute("toasts", List.of(
      Toast.success("Message sent").withDescription("We answer within one working day.")));
  return "redirect:/contact";
}
```

The page the redirect loads then renders this toast in the layout's toaster (the `th:each` above), as below. Only
here in the docs does it stay (`duration="0"`), so you can look at it; in your application it closes after the
toaster's duration like any other.

**Example: Rendered by the server.** A toast the page renders, such as a flash attribute after a redirect. duration="0" keeps this one here.

```html
<sl:toaster id="toaster-server">
  <sl:toast variant="success" title="Message sent" description="We answer within one working day."
            duration="0"/>
</sl:toaster>
```

A screen reader announces such a toast a moment after the page loads (see [Announcement](#announcement)), but that
moment is also when it starts reading the new page, and not every screen reader lets one interrupt the other. When
the outcome is the whole point of the page, say it in the page too: in the title, or in an
[alert](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/alert.md).

#### Out of band

A response that renders markup anyway can put a toast into the toaster itself, whose id is `toaster` unless you give it
another. Wrap the toasts in an element whose children a `beforeend` swap appends (an `ol` suits `li` toasts):

```html
<th:block th:fragment="invited">
  <form th:replace="~{members :: invite-form}"></form>
  <ol hx-swap-oob="beforeend:#toaster">
    <sl:toast variant="success" th:title="|Invitation sent to ${member.name}|"
              description="They get an email with a link to join the team."/>
  </ol>
</th:block>
```

A toast rendered this way can hold markup of its own, such as a link: content in `<sl:toast>` replaces the
description. Remember that the toast goes away (see [No action button](#no-action-button)).

#### From your own script

The toaster listens for the event on the document, so your own Alpine markup (or any script) can send one too:

```html
<sl:button x-data x-on:click="$dispatch('sl-toast', {title: 'Link copied'})">Copy link</sl:button>
```

The detail is a toast (`{title, description, variant, duration}`), a list of them, or a string, the title.

### Variants

The variant only changes the icon, as in shadcn: none, a check (`success`), an i (`info`), a triangle (`warning`) and
an x (`error`), whose icon takes the destructive colour. A screen reader announces an `error` at once, interrupting
what it was reading; the others when it is done. Give a toast a title that says what happened on its own ("Could not
save"), since the icon is decoration and is not read out.

**Example: Variants.** The variant sets the icon; a screen reader announces an error at once.

```html
<sl:button variant="outline" x-data x-on:click="$dispatch('sl-toast', {title: 'Event has been created'})">
  Default
</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="outline" x-data
           x-on:click="$dispatch('sl-toast', {title: 'Event has been created', variant: 'success'})">
  Success
</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="outline" x-data
           x-on:click="$dispatch('sl-toast', {title: 'Be at the area 10 minutes before the event time', variant: 'info'})">
  Info
</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="outline" x-data
           x-on:click="$dispatch('sl-toast', {title: 'Event start time cannot be earlier than 8am', variant: 'warning'})">
  Warning
</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="outline" x-data
           x-on:click="$dispatch('sl-toast', {title: 'Event has not been created', variant: 'error'})">
  Error
</sl:button>

<sl:toaster id="toaster-variants"/>
```

An icon of your own replaces the variant's:

```html
<sl:toast title="Invitation sent">
  <sl:slot name="icon"><sl:icon name="mail"/></sl:slot>
</sl:toast>
```

### Timing, pausing and closing

A toast closes after 5 seconds (`duration` on the toaster, or on one toast; `0` keeps it until it is closed). The
time stops while the pointer is on the toasts, while one of them has the focus and while the page is in another tab,
and at least a second is left afterwards, so nobody loses a toast while reading it. Choose a longer duration, or `0`,
for a toast with a long description.

- **The close button** closes one toast. It needs Alpine, so it only shows once Alpine runs; its label comes from the
  message `sl.toast.close`.
- **Alt+T** moves the focus to the newest toast, as in Sonner, from anywhere on the page; the toaster's name,
  "Notifications (Alt+T)" (message `sl.toaster.label`), tells screen reader users so. **Tab** then reaches the close
  buttons.
- **Escape** closes the toast that has the focus, and nothing else: an open dialog around it stays open.
- When the toast with the focus closes, the focus moves to the next toast, and after the last one back to where it was
  before.

### Several at once

Newer toasts stack in front of older ones, as Sonner's do; hovering or focusing them spreads them out. At most three
show (`visible-toasts`); the older ones wait, with their time stopped, and show again when a newer one closes.

**Example: Several at once.** Newer toasts stack in front; hover or focus them to spread them out, which also stops their time.

```html
<sl:button variant="outline" x-data
           x-on:click="$dispatch('sl-toast', [{title: 'Invitation sent to Ada'}, {title: 'Invitation sent to Grace'}, {title: 'Invitation sent to Alan', description: 'They get an email with a link to join the team.'}])">
  Invite three members
</sl:button>

<sl:toaster id="toaster-stack"/>
```

Where the user prefers reduced motion, toasts only fade in and out; they do not slide.

### Position

`position` puts the toasts in a corner or at the middle of the top or bottom edge: `top-left`, `top-center`,
`top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center` or `bottom-right` (the default, as Sonner's). Right and left are the end
and the start of a line, so they swap on a right-to-left page. On a narrow screen the toasts take the full width.

```html
<sl:toaster position="top-center"/>
```

### Above a modal dialog

A modal dialog makes the rest of the page inert: it can be seen but not clicked, focused or read by a screen reader,
and the dialog is drawn above everything else. The toasts are a popover (in the top layer, above everything), and while
a modal dialog is open they move into it, so a toast about something done in a dialog that stays open shows above it,
can be closed and is announced. When the dialog closes they move back. A response that closes the dialog and shows a
toast (`HX-Trigger: {"sl-dialog-close": null, "sl-toast": {...}}`) works whichever event comes first.

### Announcement

The toasts themselves are not a live region, so a screen reader does not read them twice. The toaster has two empty
live regions from the start, one polite (`role="status"`) and one assertive (`role="alert"`, for errors), and writes
each toast's title and description into one of them when it arrives. A live region has to be on the page before its
content changes for a screen reader to notice, which is why they are in the toaster's markup rather than added with
the toast; a toast rendered with the page is written into them a moment after it loads. The messages are removed from
the live regions after a few seconds, so reading the page later finds each toast once, in the "Notifications" region,
while it shows. The region is only a landmark while it holds toasts.

### Focus after the thing is gone

A toast must not take the focus: it goes away, and the focus would fall to the top of the page with it. When an action
removes the element that had the focus, such as a Delete button in a table row, move the focus to what comes next and
let the toast say what happened. The [alert dialog's htmx example](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/alert-dialog.md#confirming-with-htmx) moves it to
the next row.

### No action button

Sonner's toast can hold an action button ("Undo"). Shadleaf's has none: a toast closes by itself, and whatever it offers
is gone with it, for someone who reads slowly, uses a screen reader or looked away. WCAG asks that a time limit on
something the user has to do can be turned off or extended. Put the action in the page (an Undo in the row's place, a
link in the confirmation), and use the toast to say what happened. If a toast you render out of band holds a link, the
same must be reachable elsewhere, or give it `duration="0"`.

### Left out

- **`toast()` in the browser.** The server sends toasts; a script can dispatch `sl-toast` (see above).
- **Action and cancel buttons**, and **promise and loading toasts**: see above; a loading state belongs on the button
  that started the request.
- **Swipe to dismiss.** The close button, Escape and the time do it.
- **Rich colours** (`richColors`), **`expand`** (always spread out), **`invert`**, **`offset`** and **`gap`** as
  props: the skins set the look, and the CSS custom properties `--toaster-offset` and `--toast-gap` on
  `.toaster-viewport` the spacing.
- **Updating a toast by id.**

### Without JavaScript

Without Alpine a toast rendered with the page still shows, in its corner, but it has no close button and does not go
away; events and out-of-band toasts need htmx or a script anyway.

### Attributes

#### sl:toaster

Attributes of `<sl:toaster>`: Where toasts show: short messages in a corner of the page that close themselves, such as "Member deleted". Put one at the end of the layout's `body`. Toasts get there three ways: as `sl:toast`s inside it, which the server renders (e.g. from a flash attribute after a redirect); from an `sl-toast` event, which an htmx response sends with the `HX-Trigger` header; or swapped in out of band. A screen reader announces each toast, and toasts show above an open modal dialog and can be used there. Needs Alpine.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | *string* | `toaster` | The toaster's id, which an out-of-band swap targets (`hx-swap-oob="beforeend:#toaster"`). |
| `position` | `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, `bottom-right` | `bottom-right` | The corner or edge the toasts show in. `right` and `left` are the end and the start of a line. |
| `duration` | *number* | `5000` | How long a toast shows, in milliseconds, unless it sets its own. The time stops while the pointer is on the toasts, while one of them has the focus and while the page is hidden. `0` keeps toasts until they are closed. |
| `visible-toasts` | *number* | `3` | How many toasts show at once, the newest ones. Older ones wait, with their time stopped, and show again when a newer one closes. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:id="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:toast

Attributes of `<sl:toast>`: One toast in a `sl:toaster`: a title, an optional description and a close button. The server renders it for a message that has to show when the page loads, such as a flash attribute after a redirect, or in an out-of-band swap. Content of its own replaces the description. A toast goes away by itself, so it must never hold the only way to do something.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | *string* | **required** | What happened, in a few words: "Member deleted". |
| `description` | *string* | — | More about it, under the title. |
| `variant` | `default`, `success`, `info`, `warning`, `error` | `default` | The kind of message, shown by its icon: none, a check, an i, a warning triangle or an x. A screen reader announces an `error` at once, interrupting what it reads; the others when it is done. |
| `duration` | *number* | — | How long this toast shows, in milliseconds, instead of the toaster's `duration`. `0` keeps it until it is closed. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:title="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

### JavaScript

A small Alpine component, `slToaster`, is on `<sl:toaster>`: it renders as
`<div class="toaster" x-data="slToaster">`.

- **It needs no Alpine plugin.** If you load Alpine yourself (`shadleaf.assets.alpine=external`), plain Alpine is
  enough. See [Alpine](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/alpine.md).
- **Keep your own `x-data` off `<sl:toaster>`.** An element has one `x-data`.
- **One toaster per page.** A second one works, but the first takes every event.
- **htmx history:** the toaster removes its toasts before htmx saves the page in its history cache, so going back never
  shows an old toast again.

| Event | On | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sl-toast` | anything (it bubbles to the document), or the document | Shows the toast in its detail: `{title, description, variant, duration}`, a list of them, or a string. |

---

## Skeleton

> A placeholder that pulses while content loads.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/skeleton/

**Example: Skeleton.**

```html
<sl:skeleton/>
<sl:skeleton/>
```

### Shapes and sizes

A skeleton is a line of text by default: the full width of its container and one line high. `shape="circle"` stands in
for an avatar. Both are starting points: give a skeleton the size of what it replaces with a class of your own, for
example `class="h-32 w-64"` when your application compiles Tailwind. Your class wins over the skin's size.

**Example: In a card.** The card that is loading says so with aria-busy; the skeletons are hidden from assistive technology.

```html
<sl:card aria-busy="true">
  <sl:card-header>
    <sl:skeleton shape="circle"/>
  </sl:card-header>
  <sl:card-content>
    <sl:skeleton/>
    <sl:skeleton/>
  </sl:card-content>
</sl:card>
```

### While it loads

A skeleton is only a picture of content to come, so it is hidden from assistive technology (`aria-hidden="true"`).
Put `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is loading, and remove it when the content arrives, for example when htmx
swaps it in. The pulse stops for users who ask for reduced motion.

### Attributes

Attributes of `<sl:skeleton>`: A placeholder that pulses while content loads. It is hidden from assistive technology; mark the region that is loading with `aria-busy="true"` instead. Give it the size of what it stands in for with a class of your own.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | `line`, `circle` | `line` | A line of text (full width, one line high) or a circle (an avatar). |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:shape="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

---

## Spinner

> A spinning icon that says something is loading.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/spinner/

**Example: Spinner.**

```html
<sl:spinner/>
```

### What it says

A spinner is a status (`role="status"`) named "Loading". Give it an `aria-label` of its own to say what is loading;
the default is the message `sl.spinner.label`, which you can reword or translate in your `messages.properties`.

**Example: Saying what loads.** An aria-label replaces the default name, "Loading".

```html
<sl:spinner aria-label="Loading invoices"/>
```

For a button that is busy, use [`<sl:button loading>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/button.md) instead: it shows the spinner, disables the button
and announces the busy state. To show a skeleton of the content to come, use [`<sl:skeleton>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/skeleton.md).

### Sizes

A spinner is 16 pixels, or the size of an icon in the component around it, such as
[`<sl:empty-media variant="icon">`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/empty.md#while-it-loads). `size` sets the width and height in pixels.

**Example: Sizes.**

```html
<sl:spinner/>
<sl:spinner size="24"/>
<sl:spinner size="32"/>
```

### Reduced motion

For users who ask for reduced motion the spinner turns slower instead of standing still: a frozen arc reads as a
broken icon.

### Attributes

Attributes of `<sl:spinner>`: A spinning icon that says something is loading: a status (`role="status"`) named "Loading" (the message `sl.spinner.label`; an `aria-label` of its own replaces it). It turns slower, not still, when the user asks for reduced motion. For a button that is busy, use `sl:button loading` instead.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | *number* | — | Width and height in pixels. Without it the spinner is 16 pixels, or sized by the surrounding component (as an icon in `sl:empty-media`). |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:size="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

---

## Empty

> What a list, a table, a search or a page shows when there is nothing to show yet.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/empty/

**Example: Empty.**

```html
<sl:empty>
  <sl:empty-header>
    <sl:empty-media variant="icon"><sl:icon name="folder-code"/></sl:empty-media>
    <sl:empty-title level="3">No projects yet</sl:empty-title>
    <sl:empty-description>You haven't created any projects yet. Get started by creating your first
      project.</sl:empty-description>
  </sl:empty-header>
  <sl:empty-content>
    <sl:button as="a" href="/projects/new">Create project</sl:button>
  </sl:empty-content>
  <sl:button as="a" href="/docs/projects" variant="link" size="sm">
    Learn more
    <sl:slot name="icon-end"><sl:icon name="arrow-up-right"/></sl:slot>
  </sl:button>
</sl:empty>
```

### Built from parts

An empty state is `<sl:empty>` plus the parts you need, as in shadcn/ui: `<sl:empty-header>` (holding
`<sl:empty-media>`, `<sl:empty-title>` and `<sl:empty-description>`) and `<sl:empty-content>` for what to do next, such
as a button, a search field or a link. Everything is centred, and the empty state grows to fill a flex container, so
it sits in the middle of the space it is given.

`<sl:empty-media variant="icon">` puts an icon on a muted square. The default media shows its content as it is, for an
avatar or an image.

**Example: With an avatar.** The default media shows its content as it is.

```html
<sl:empty>
  <sl:empty-header>
    <sl:empty-media>
      <sl:avatar size="lg" label="Ada Lovelace">
        <sl:avatar-image th:src="@{/users/{id}/photo(id=${user.id})}"/>
        <sl:avatar-fallback>AL</sl:avatar-fallback>
      </sl:avatar>
    </sl:empty-media>
    <sl:empty-title level="3">User offline</sl:empty-title>
    <sl:empty-description>This user is currently offline. You can leave a message to notify them or try
      again later.</sl:empty-description>
  </sl:empty-header>
  <sl:empty-content>
    <sl:button size="sm">Leave message</sl:button>
  </sl:empty-content>
</sl:empty>
```

### A title that is a heading

`<sl:empty-title>` is plain text unless you give it a `level`. With one, it is announced as a heading of that level.
Pick the level that fits the page: an empty state under an `<h2>` gets `level="3"`.

### Outline

`border` draws a dashed line around the empty state, to mark out the area. It works without utility classes, so also
with the standalone stylesheet.

**Example: Outline.** border draws a dashed line around the empty state.

```html
<sl:empty border>
  <sl:empty-header>
    <sl:empty-media variant="icon"><sl:icon name="cloud"/></sl:empty-media>
    <sl:empty-title level="3">Cloud storage is empty</sl:empty-title>
    <sl:empty-description>Upload files to your cloud storage to access them anywhere.</sl:empty-description>
  </sl:empty-header>
  <sl:empty-content>
    <sl:button variant="outline" size="sm">Upload files</sl:button>
  </sl:empty-content>
</sl:empty>
```

### In a card

**Example: In a card.**

```html
<sl:card>
  <sl:card-header>
    <sl:card-title level="3">Projects</sl:card-title>
    <sl:card-description>Everything your team is working on</sl:card-description>
  </sl:card-header>
  <sl:card-content>
    <sl:empty>
      <sl:empty-header>
        <sl:empty-media variant="icon"><sl:icon name="folder"/></sl:empty-media>
        <sl:empty-title level="4">No projects yet</sl:empty-title>
        <sl:empty-description>Create a project to start working with your team.</sl:empty-description>
      </sl:empty-header>
      <sl:empty-content>
        <sl:button as="a" href="/projects/new">Create project</sl:button>
      </sl:empty-content>
    </sl:empty>
  </sl:card-content>
</sl:card>
```

### In an empty table

Put the empty state in [`<sl:table-empty>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md), which spans every column: it replaces the row's
"No results." text.

**Example: In an empty table.** An sl:empty as the content of sl:table-empty replaces its "No results." text.

```html
<sl:table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Name</th>
      <th>Email</th>
      <th>Role</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr th:each="person : ${people}">
      <td th:text="${person.name}">Ada Lovelace</td>
      <td th:text="${person.email}">ada@example.com</td>
      <td th:text="${person.role}">Owner</td>
    </tr>
    <sl:table-empty colspan="3" th:if="${people.empty}">
      <sl:empty>
        <sl:empty-header>
          <sl:empty-media variant="icon"><sl:icon name="users"/></sl:empty-media>
          <sl:empty-title level="3">No people yet</sl:empty-title>
          <sl:empty-description>Invite your team to collaborate on this project.</sl:empty-description>
        </sl:empty-header>
        <sl:empty-content>
          <sl:button as="a" href="/people/invite" size="sm">
            <sl:slot name="icon-start"><sl:icon name="plus"/></sl:slot>
            Invite people
          </sl:button>
        </sl:empty-content>
      </sl:empty>
    </sl:table-empty>
  </tbody>
</sl:table>
```

### With a search field

A link in a description is underlined. An `<sl:empty-description>` can also go in the content, below the field.

**Example: With a search field.** Links in the description are underlined.

```html
<sl:empty>
  <sl:empty-header>
    <sl:empty-title level="3">404 - Not found</sl:empty-title>
    <sl:empty-description>The page you're looking for doesn't exist. Try searching for what you need
      below.</sl:empty-description>
  </sl:empty-header>
  <sl:empty-content>
    <form action="/search" role="search" aria-label="Pages">
      <sl:input-group>
        <sl:input-group-input type="search" name="pageQuery" placeholder="Try searching for pages..."
                              aria-label="Search pages"/>
        <sl:input-group-addon><sl:icon name="search"/></sl:input-group-addon>
      </sl:input-group>
    </form>
    <sl:empty-description>Need help? <a href="/support">Contact support</a></sl:empty-description>
  </sl:empty-content>
</sl:empty>
```

### While it loads

An [`<sl:spinner>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/spinner.md) takes the icon's place in the media while something loads.

**Example: With a spinner.** While something loads, an sl:spinner takes the icon's place.

```html
<sl:empty>
  <sl:empty-header>
    <sl:empty-media variant="icon"><sl:spinner/></sl:empty-media>
    <sl:empty-title level="3">Processing your request</sl:empty-title>
    <sl:empty-description>Please wait while we process your request. Do not refresh the
      page.</sl:empty-description>
  </sl:empty-header>
  <sl:empty-content>
    <sl:button variant="outline" size="sm">Cancel</sl:button>
  </sl:empty-content>
</sl:empty>
```

### Attributes

#### sl:empty

Attributes of `<sl:empty>`: An empty state: what a list, a table, a search or a page shows when there is nothing to show yet. Holds an `sl:empty-header` (media, title and description) and an optional `sl:empty-content` with what to do next, centred in the space it is given.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `border` | *boolean* | — | A dashed line around the empty state, to mark out the area (shadcn's `border border-dashed` classes). |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:border="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:empty-header

Attributes of `<sl:empty-header>`: The top of an `sl:empty`: an optional `sl:empty-media`, an `sl:empty-title` and an `sl:empty-description`, stacked and centred.

`sl:empty-header` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:empty-media

Attributes of `<sl:empty-media>`: An icon, an avatar or an image above the title of an `sl:empty`, inside `sl:empty-header`.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `default`, `icon` | `default` | `icon` puts an icon on a muted square; `default` shows the content as it is, e.g. an avatar. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:variant="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:empty-title

Attributes of `<sl:empty-title>`: The title of an `sl:empty`, inside `sl:empty-header`.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6` | — | Heading level. With it the title is a heading (`role="heading"` and `aria-level`) that screen reader users can jump to; without it, plain text. Pick the level that fits the page's outline. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:level="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:empty-description

Attributes of `<sl:empty-description>`: The text below the title of an `sl:empty`. Links in it are underlined.

`sl:empty-description` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:empty-content

Attributes of `<sl:empty-content>`: What to do next in an `sl:empty`, below its header: a button, a search field, a link.

`sl:empty-content` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

---

## Table

> A table in shadcn/ui's look, whose column headers sort it on the server.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table/

**Example: Table.**

```html
<sl:table>
  <caption>A list of your recent invoices.</caption>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Invoice</th>
      <th>Status</th>
      <th>Method</th>
      <sl:table-head align="end">Amount</sl:table-head>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>INV001</td>
      <td><sl:badge variant="secondary">Paid</sl:badge></td>
      <td>Credit card</td>
      <td data-align="end">€250.00</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>INV002</td>
      <td><sl:badge variant="outline">Pending</sl:badge></td>
      <td>Bank transfer</td>
      <td data-align="end">€150.00</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>INV003</td>
      <td><sl:badge variant="destructive">Overdue</sl:badge></td>
      <td>Credit card</td>
      <td data-align="end">€350.00</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
  <tfoot>
    <tr>
      <td colspan="3">Total</td>
      <td data-align="end">€750.00</td>
    </tr>
  </tfoot>
</sl:table>
```

### Plain rows and cells

`<sl:table>` styles the plain table elements you write inside it: `caption`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `th` and
`td`. There is no component per row or cell, as there is in shadcn/ui, so a row is the `th:each` you already write:

```html
<sl:table>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Name</th><th>Email</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr th:each="person : ${people}">
      <td th:text="${person.name}">Ada Lovelace</td>
      <td th:text="${person.email}">ada@example.com</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</sl:table>
```

Attributes on `<sl:table>` go to the `table`; it sits in a container that scrolls sideways when the table is wider
than the page. A table nested in a cell keeps its own look, so put it in an `<sl:table>` of its own.

### Alignment

`<sl:table-head align="end">` puts a header's label at the end of its cell. The cells below take the same with
`data-align="end"` (or `"center"`), which works without utility classes, so also with the standalone stylesheet. Use
it for amounts and other numbers, so their digits line up.

### Wide tables

A table wider than the page scrolls sideways inside its container. A keyboard user can scroll it too: Chromium and
Firefox make the container a tab stop of its own when nothing in it can take the focus, and the arrow keys then scroll
it; when a sort link, a checkbox or a row's menu button in it takes the focus, the browser scrolls it into view. The
container has no `tabindex` of its own, which would add a tab stop to every table that fits.

WebKit, checked with Playwright's build of it, does neither for a container of plain text: there a wide table with
nothing to focus in it cannot be reached with the keyboard, and with Option+Tab (Safari's *Press Tab to highlight each
item*) its links can, as above. axe reports such a table as
`scrollable-region-focusable`. Keep a table that is only text from growing wider than a phone, or give its rows
something to focus.

### Sorting on the server

The rows of a Spring application live on the server, which sends one page of them. So a sortable header is a link that
asks the server for the page in another order, not a script that reorders the rows in the browser:

**Example: Sorted on the server.** Sorted by name, in a request for /people?q=a&sort=name,asc. Each link keeps q.

```html
<sl:table th:page="${people}">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <sl:table-head sort="name">Name</sl:table-head>
      <sl:table-head sort="email">Email</sl:table-head>
      <sl:table-head sort="orders" align="end">Orders</sl:table-head>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr th:each="person : ${people}">
      <td th:text="${person.name}">Ada Lovelace</td>
      <td th:text="${person.email}">ada@example.com</td>
      <td data-align="end" th:text="${person.orders}">3</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</sl:table>
```

`<sl:table-head sort="name">` links to the same page with `sort=name,asc`, or `sort=name,desc` when the table is
sorted by name ascending already. The link keeps every other parameter in the address (a search, the page size) and
drops the page number, so a new order starts on the first page. The sorted column gets `aria-sort`, which screen
readers announce, and an arrow; the others show both chevrons. A click on the sorted column reverses it; there is no
unsorted state, because the default order is the controller's.

The controller takes a `Pageable`, which Spring Data fills from those parameters, and puts the page in the model:

```java
@GetMapping("/people")
String people(@PageableDefault(sort = "name") Pageable pageable, Model model) {
  model.addAttribute("people", personRepository.findAll(pageable));
  return "people";
}
```

```html
<sl:table th:page="${people}">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <sl:table-head sort="name">Name</sl:table-head>
      <sl:table-head sort="email">Email</sl:table-head>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  ...
</sl:table>
```

`th:page` takes the `Page` (or `Slice`), whose `Sort` tells the headers how the rows are sorted, the default from
`@PageableDefault` included. Only the first sort key is shown. `spring-data-commons` is all it needs, not a Spring Data
module: rows that do not come from a repository can be wrapped in a
`new PageImpl<>(rows, pageable, total)`.

Without `th:page` the headers read the order from the request's `sort` parameter, so a table sorts without Spring Data
too; the controller then reads that parameter itself.

#### Parameter names

The links use the parameter names your `Pageable` reads. Shadleaf takes them from Spring Boot's properties:
`spring.data.web.sort.sort-parameter`, and for the page and size links
`spring.data.web.pageable.page-parameter`, `size-parameter`, `prefix`, `qualifier-delimiter` and
`one-indexed-parameters`. If you configure Spring Data's resolvers in code instead, declare a `PagingParameters` bean
with the same values.

#### Two tables on one page

Two sortable tables on one page need their own parameters. Give the controller's second `Pageable` a `@Qualifier`, and
the table the same `qualifier`:

```java
@GetMapping("/team")
String team(Pageable pageable, @Qualifier("members") Pageable members, Model model) { ... }
```

```html
<sl:table th:page="${members}" qualifier="members"> ... </sl:table>
```

Its headers then link to `members_sort=email,asc` and leave the other table's `sort` and `page` alone.

#### Limit what can be sorted

The sort parameter is part of the address, so anyone can edit it. Spring Data passes an unknown property on to the
repository, which fails with an error page (`?sort=password` is an error at best). So the controller checks the order
against the columns the table offers before it queries, and falls back to the default order when it asks for anything
else:

```java
@Controller
class PeopleController {

  // The properties of the table's <sl:table-head sort="..."> columns.
  private static final Set<String> SORTABLE = Set.of("name", "email", "orders");

  private final PersonRepository personRepository;

  PeopleController(PersonRepository personRepository) {
    this.personRepository = personRepository;
  }

  @GetMapping("/people")
  String people(@PageableDefault(sort = "name") Pageable pageable, Model model) {
    model.addAttribute("people", personRepository.findAll(sortable(pageable)));
    return "people";
  }

  /** The pageable as requested, or sorted by name when it names a property the table does not offer. */
  private static Pageable sortable(Pageable pageable) {
    boolean allowed = pageable.getSort().stream().allMatch(order -> SORTABLE.contains(order.getProperty()));
    return allowed
        ? pageable
        : PageRequest.of(pageable.getPageNumber(), pageable.getPageSize(), Sort.by("name"));
  }
}
```

The page the repository returns carries the order it was sorted by, so the table shows the fallback correctly too.

#### A stable order across pages

Rows with the same value in the sorted column (two people with 59 orders) come back from the database in no particular
order, and not necessarily the same one for every page. Once the table has [pages](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/pagination.md), such a row can
show up on two pages, or on none. Add a unique key the reader does not see, such as the id, as the last sort key before
you query:

```java
@GetMapping("/people")
String people(@PageableDefault(sort = "name") Pageable pageable, Model model) {
  Pageable stable = PageRequest.of(pageable.getPageNumber(), pageable.getPageSize(),
      sortable(pageable).getSort().and(Sort.by("id")));
  model.addAttribute("people", personRepository.findAll(stable));
  return "people";
}
```

The headers show only the first sort key, and the links are built from the request rather than from the page's
`Sort`, so the id never shows up in the address. Sample-01's `/people` page does this, and its test follows Next from
the first page to the last and finds every person exactly once.

#### Sorting an enum column

An enum stored as a string (`@Enumerated(EnumType.STRING)`) sorts alphabetically: Admin, Guest, Member, Owner. To sort
roles by rank, sort the database by the rank:

- **Store the rank.** An `AttributeConverter` writes the enum as a number, so `sort=role` sorts by rank and the header
  needs nothing else. Sample-01 does this:

  ```java
  public enum Role {
    OWNER(1), ADMIN(2), MEMBER(3), GUEST(4);
    ...
  }

  @Converter
  class RoleConverter implements AttributeConverter<Role, Integer> {
    public Integer convertToDatabaseColumn(Role role) { return role == null ? null : role.getRank(); }
    public Role convertToEntityAttribute(Integer rank) { return rank == null ? null : Role.ofRank(rank); }
  }
  ```

  ```java
  @Convert(converter = RoleConverter.class)
  private Role role;
  ```

  An explicit rank, unlike `EnumType.ORDINAL`, survives reordering the enum's constants.
- **Sort by an expression.** Keep the string column and order by a `CASE` expression in a query of your own
  (`order by case p.role when 'OWNER' then 1 when 'ADMIN' then 2 ... end`), or with `JpaSort.unsafe(...)`. The
  controller then maps the `role` property of the requested `Sort` to that expression, and the `Page` it gets back
  carries the expression, not `role`: build the page the template gets with the requested `Pageable`
  (`new PageImpl<>(page.getContent(), pageable, page.getTotalElements())`) so the header still shows the order.

#### Focus after an htmx swap

Each sort link has an id (`sort-name`, or `members-sort-name` with a qualifier), so when htmx replaces the table it
gives the focus back to the link that was clicked. [Tables with htmx](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tables-htmx.md) puts it together.

### Search and filters

A search or filter above the table is a `GET` form the controller reads (`?q=ada`). Put
[`<sl:query-params except="q"/>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/query-params.md) in it, so sending it keeps the table's order and page size and
starts on the first page; the sort and page links keep `q` by themselves. To search as the user types, see
[Tables with htmx](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tables-htmx.md).

### Nothing found

`<sl:table-empty>` is the row to show when there are no rows: one cell across the table's `colspan` columns, saying
"No results." (the message `sl.table.empty`, which your `messages.properties` can reword). Content of its own replaces
the text.

**Example: Nothing found.**

```html
<sl:table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Name</th>
      <th>Email</th>
      <th>Role</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr th:each="person : ${people}">
      <td th:text="${person.name}">Ada Lovelace</td>
      <td th:text="${person.email}">ada@example.com</td>
      <td th:text="${person.role}">Owner</td>
    </tr>
    <sl:table-empty colspan="3" th:if="${people.empty}"/>
  </tbody>
</sl:table>
```

```html
<sl:table-empty colspan="3" th:if="${people.empty}">Nobody matches your search.</sl:table-empty>
```

### Actions per row

Put a [dropdown menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/dropdown-menu.md) in the last cell, as shadcn's data table does. Give each menu an id built
from its row, so every trigger has a stable id of its own (`people-12-actions-trigger`), and name the trigger after the
row: a screen reader user tabbing through the table hears "Actions for Ada Lovelace, menu button". The header cell
above the menus needs a name too, read out with each cell: `<span class="sl-sr-only">Actions</span>`.

**Example: Actions per row.** A menu in the last cell of each row, named after its row. In an application its items post or link (see Tables with htmx); here they do nothing.

```html
<sl:table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Name</th>
      <th>Role</th>
      <th data-align="end"><span class="sl-sr-only">Actions</span></th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr th:each="person : ${people}">
      <td th:text="${person.name}">Ada Lovelace</td>
      <td><sl:badge variant="secondary" th:text="${person.role.label}">Owner</sl:badge></td>
      <td data-align="end">
        <!--/* A role="menu" holds menu items only, so the form goes around the menu. */-->
        <form method="post" th:action="${selfUrl}">
          <input type="hidden" name="person" th:value="${person.id}">
          <sl:dropdown-menu th:id="|people-${person.id}-actions|">
            <sl:dropdown-menu-trigger variant="ghost" size="icon-sm"
                                      th:aria-label="|Actions for ${person.name}|">
              <sl:icon name="ellipsis"/>
            </sl:dropdown-menu-trigger>
            <sl:dropdown-menu-content align="end">
              <sl:dropdown-menu-item as="a" th:href="@{/people/{id}(id=${person.id})}">
                <sl:icon name="eye"/>View
              </sl:dropdown-menu-item>
              <sl:dropdown-menu-separator/>
              <sl:dropdown-menu-label>Change role</sl:dropdown-menu-label>
              <sl:dropdown-menu-radio-group aria-label="Change role">
                <sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item th:each="role : ${roles}" type="submit" name="role"
                                             th:value="${role}" th:checked="${person.role == role}">
                  [[${role.label}]]
                </sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item>
              </sl:dropdown-menu-radio-group>
              <sl:dropdown-menu-separator/>
              <sl:dropdown-menu-item as="a" variant="destructive"
                                     th:href="@{/people/{id}/delete(id=${person.id})}">
                <sl:icon name="trash-2"/>Delete
              </sl:dropdown-menu-item>
            </sl:dropdown-menu-content>
          </sl:dropdown-menu>
        </form>
      </td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</sl:table>
```

An item that changes something is a submit button of a `post` form. A `role="menu"` may only hold menu items, so the
form goes around the menu: a hidden input names the row, and each item sends its own `name` and `value` (`role=ADMIN`).
View is a link; Delete is a link to a page that asks first. [Tables with htmx](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tables-htmx.md#actions-per-row)
turns the same menu into htmx requests, with an alert dialog for Delete, and keeps the focus on the row's menu button.

A menu per row is markup per row: 50 rows with a badge and the menu above render in about 9 ms and 222 KB of HTML,
5 KB once compressed (see [the cost](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tables-htmx.md#the-cost-of-a-menu-per-row)).

### Selecting rows

For a bulk action (delete, change a role), give each row a checkbox of your own and put
`<sl:table-select-all/>` in the header cell above them. Select-all checks or unchecks every row on the page, and is
checked when they all are, indeterminate (a minus) when some are. `<sl:table-selection-count>` says how many are
selected; place it where it fits, e.g. at the start of the footer, as shadcn's data table does.

**Example: Selecting rows.** The rows are plain checkboxes named ids; one is selected, so select-all starts indeterminate.

```html
<sl:table id="people-selection">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th><sl:table-select-all/></th>
      <th>Name</th>
      <th>Email</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr th:each="person : ${people}">
      <td><sl:checkbox name="ids" th:value="${person.id}"
                       th:aria-label="#{sl.table.select-row(${person.name})}"/></td>
      <td th:text="${person.name}">Ada Lovelace</td>
      <td th:text="${person.email}">ada@example.com</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</sl:table>
<sl:table-selection-count for="people-selection"/>
```

```html
<form id="people-bulk" method="post" th:action="${selfUrl}">
  <sl:table id="people-table" th:page="${people}">
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th><sl:table-select-all/></th>
        <sl:table-head sort="name">Name</sl:table-head>
        <sl:table-head sort="email">Email</sl:table-head>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr th:each="person : ${people}">
        <td><sl:checkbox name="ids" th:value="${person.id}"
                         th:aria-label="#{sl.table.select-row(${person.name})}"/></td>
        <td th:text="${person.name}">Ada Lovelace</td>
        <td th:text="${person.email}">ada@example.com</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </sl:table>
  <sl:button type="submit" variant="destructive">Delete selected</sl:button>
</form>
<div class="table-footer">
  <sl:table-selection-count for="people-table"/>
  <sl:pagination th:page="${people}"/>
</div>
```

- **The rows are yours.** Plain `sl:checkbox`es (`name="ids"`, the row's id as value) submit with the form, also
  without JavaScript; the controller gets `@RequestParam List<Long> ids`. The table can sit inside the form, or the
  checkboxes can name a form elsewhere with `form="..."`.
- **Which checkboxes are rows.** Select-all works on the checkboxes in the body cells of the table it is in (not of a
  table nested in a cell), leaving out disabled ones, which would not be submitted. When the body has other
  checkboxes too, `name="ids"` on select-all narrows it to those.
- **The selected look** comes from CSS: a row whose first cell holds a checked checkbox gets the muted background
  (shadcn's `data-state="selected"`), with or without JavaScript. Put the selection in the first column.
- **Names.** Every row checkbox needs an accessible name, telling the rows apart. `aria-label` with the message
  `sl.table.select-row` (`Select {0}`) as above, or point at the cell that names the row:

  ```html
  <td><sl:checkbox name="ids" th:value="${person.id}"
                   th:aria-labelledby="|person-${person.id}-name|"/></td>
  <td th:id="|person-${person.id}-name|" th:text="${person.name}">Ada Lovelace</td>
  ```

  Select-all is named "Select all rows on this page" (`sl.table.select-all`); an `aria-label` of yours replaces it.
- **The count** reads "2 of 20 selected" (`sl.table.selection.count`; keep `{0}` and `{1}` as they are, the browser
  fills them in). Its `table` prop is the table's `id`, which `sl:table` puts on the `table`. It is not a live region:
  a row's checkbox announces its own state, so the count is only announced after a click on select-all, which
  changes rows the user did not touch.

#### Without JavaScript

Select-all and the count need Alpine, so they keep their place but stay hidden until it starts (`x-cloak`). Without
JavaScript the user checks the rows one by one, and the form submits them as before.

#### The bulk action

Post the form to the page's own URL, query string included, so the action knows the search, order and page to come
back to. The controller below puts that URL in the model; after the action it redirects back there with a toast
(post/redirect/get):

```java
@PostMapping("/people")
public String delete(@RequestParam(name = "ids", required = false) List<Long> ids,
    HttpServletRequest request, RedirectAttributes redirectAttributes) {
  repository.deleteAllByIdInBatch(ids == null ? List.of() : ids);
  redirectAttributes.addFlashAttribute("toasts", List.of(Toast.success("People deleted")));
  String query = request.getQueryString();
  return "redirect:/people" + (query == null ? "" : "?" + query);
}
```

Ask before a destructive action with an [alert dialog](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/alert-dialog.md) inside the form: its destructive button is a
submit button. With htmx, answer with the table alone; [Tables with htmx](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tables-htmx.md#selection-and-a-bulk-action)
shows how, and sample-01's `/people-multiselect` page does both.

#### Selection across pages

Select-all selects the rows on the page, and a sort, another page or a new search (with htmx too) starts with nothing
selected: the selection lives in the checkboxes, and those are replaced. Keeping it across pages is the server's
business. Two ways:

- **Keep the ids on the server**, e.g. in the session: each page posts its selection (or a checkbox posts on change
  with htmx), and the page renders `checked` on the rows that were selected before. Select-all and the count then
  start from those.
- **Select everything that matches** instead of ids: after select-all, offer "Select all 270 people", which posts the
  search itself (`q`) for the action to apply to every match.

Sample-01 keeps the selection per page.

#### JavaScript

`<sl:table-select-all>` renders `x-data="slTableSelection"` and `<sl:table-selection-count>`
`x-data="slTableSelectionCount"`. They need no Alpine plugin. They follow the rows' `change` events (Space or a click),
a form reset, and rows being added or replaced (an htmx swap). Changing the rows from select-all fires `input` and
`change` on every row it changes, as a click would.

| Event | On | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sl-table-selection-change` | the `table`, bubbling | `{selected, total}`, after every change, and when select-all starts |

A bulk action can listen to it, for instance to show how many people it would delete:

```html
<div x-data="{selected: 0}" @sl-table-selection-change.document="selected = $event.detail.selected">...</div>
```

A checkbox of your own can be indeterminate too: set its `indeterminate` property, or render
[`<sl:checkbox indeterminate>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/checkbox.md#indeterminate).

### Left out

shadcn's data table runs TanStack Table in the browser. These parts of it are not in Shadleaf: sorting and filtering
in the browser, column visibility, resizing, reordering and pinning, drag handles, expandable rows, editable cells,
virtual scrolling, selecting a range of rows with Shift and a click, and a selection that lasts across pages (see
above).

### Attributes

#### sl:table

Attributes of `<sl:table>`: A table in shadcn/ui's look. Write the plain table elements inside it (`caption`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tfoot`, `tr`, `th`, `td`), with `th:each` on a row; there is no component per row or cell. Use `sl:table-head` for a header cell that sorts or aligns, and `sl:table-empty` for the row that says nothing was found. The table scrolls sideways inside its own container when it is wider than the page. Attributes go to the `table`.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `th:page` | *object* | — | The Spring Data `Page` or `Slice` the table shows. Its `Sort` tells every `sl:table-head` inside how the rows are sorted now. Without it, the headers read the order from the request's sort parameter. |
| `qualifier` | *string* | — | The `@Qualifier` of the controller's `Pageable`, for a second table on the page: its sort links use `members_sort` instead of `sort`. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:page="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:table-head

Attributes of `<sl:table-head>`: A header cell (`th`) of a `sl:table`. With `sort` its label is a link that sorts the table by that property on the server: ascending, or descending when it is sorted ascending already. The link keeps the request's other parameters (filters, page size) and goes back to the first page. The sorted column gets `aria-sort` and an arrow. A plain `th` works too, for a header that does neither.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sort` | *string* | — | The property to sort by, as the controller's `Sort` names it (`name`, `address.city`). Only the first key of the current order is shown. |
| `align` | `start`, `center`, `end` | `start` | Where the label sits in the cell. Put the same `data-align` on the column's `td`s: `end` for amounts. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:sort="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:table-empty

Attributes of `<sl:table-empty>`: The row a `sl:table` shows when there are no rows to show: one cell across every column saying "No results." (the message `sl.table.empty`). Content of its own replaces the text. Render it with `th:if`, e.g. `th:if="${people.empty}"`.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colspan` | *number* | **required** | The number of columns the cell spans: all of the table's. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:colspan="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:table-select-all

Attributes of `<sl:table-select-all>`: A checkbox for a header cell of a `sl:table` that selects every row on the page. The rows are the application's own checkboxes (a `sl:checkbox` with `name="ids"` and `th:value="${person.id}"`) in the cells of the table's body; they submit without JavaScript. This one is checked when every row is, indeterminate when some are, and checks or unchecks them all when clicked; it is named "Select all rows on this page" (the message `sl.table.select-all`) unless it gets an `aria-label`. It needs JavaScript, so it stays hidden until Alpine starts. It fires `sl-table-selection-change` on the table (`{selected, total}`), which `sl:table-selection-count` shows. It submits nothing itself (no `name`); other attributes go to its `input`, `class` to its wrapper.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | *string* | — | The `name` of the row checkboxes, when the body has checkboxes of another kind too. Without it, every checkbox in a body cell is a row. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:name="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:table-selection-count

Attributes of `<sl:table-selection-count>`: How many rows of a `sl:table` are selected: "2 of 20 selected" (the message `sl.table.selection.count`), kept up to date in the browser as rows are checked, as rows are replaced (an htmx swap) and after a form reset. Place it anywhere, e.g. at the start of the table's footer as shadcn/ui's data table does. It is not a live region: a click on `sl:table-select-all` announces the count, a row's checkbox announces its own state. Empty and hidden until Alpine starts.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `for` | *string* | **required** | The `id` of the table whose rows it counts (`sl:table` puts its `id` on the `table`). |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:for="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

---

## Pagination

> Links to the other pages of a list, built from the Spring Data Page the controller returns.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/pagination/

**Example: From a page.** Page 5 of 27, in a request for /people?sort=name,asc&page=4. Each link keeps the sort.

```html
<sl:pagination th:page="${people}"/>
```

### From a page

Give `<sl:pagination>` the Spring Data `Page` the controller put in the model, and nothing else:

```html
<sl:pagination th:page="${people}"/>
```

It renders Previous, the first and the last page, the current page with one page on each side, an ellipsis for the
pages it leaves out, and Next. A gap of a single page shows that page instead of an ellipsis, which would take the same
room. `siblings` sets how many pages show on each side of the current one:

**Example: More pages around the current one.**

```html
<sl:pagination th:page="${orders}" siblings="2" qualifier="orders" aria-label="Order pages"/>
```

Each link is the request that rendered the page with another page number: every other parameter in the address (the
sort, the page size, a search) is kept as it was. The controller needs nothing new, as the `Pageable` that sorts the
[table](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md) also reads the page:

```java
@GetMapping("/people")
String people(@PageableDefault(size = 20, sort = "name") Pageable pageable, Model model) {
  model.addAttribute("people", personRepository.findAll(pageable));
  return "people";
}
```

Sort the rows by a unique key last, or a row can show up on two pages or on none: see
[a stable order across pages](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md#a-stable-order-across-pages).

The page shown now is an outline button with `aria-current="page"`. On the first page Previous is disabled, and on the
last page Next, the way a disabled link button is: no `href`, `aria-disabled="true"`, out of the tab order. An empty
result still has one page, the one saying so.

**Example: On the first page.** Previous is disabled. A gap of one page shows that page rather than an ellipsis.

```html
<sl:pagination th:page="${team}" qualifier="team" aria-label="Team pages"/>
```

#### A Slice

A `Slice` knows whether there is a next page, not how many pages there are, so it gets Previous and Next only. It
saves the count query on a large table:

**Example: A Slice.** A Slice does not know how many pages there are, so it gets Previous and Next only.

```html
<sl:pagination th:page="${activity}" qualifier="activity" aria-label="Activity pages"/>
```

A list read a `Slice` at a time can also grow instead: [Load more](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tables-htmx.md#load-more) appends the
next slice's rows with htmx, and is a link to the next page without it.

#### Without Spring Data

Without a `Page`, pass the page shown now (counting from 1) and the number of pages:

**Example: Without Spring Data.**

```html
<sl:pagination th:current="${results.page}" th:total="${results.pages}" qualifier="results"
               aria-label="Result pages"/>
```

The links ask for the page with the same parameter Spring Data would read, zero-based unless
`spring.data.web.pageable.one-indexed-parameters` is set (see [parameter names](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md#parameter-names)); the
controller reads it itself. `sl:pagination-summary` and `sl:pagination-size` need a `Page` or `Slice`: without Spring
Data, write the summary with `#messages` and the sizes as links of your own.

#### Two lists on one page

The `qualifier` of the controller's second `Pageable` (`@Qualifier("members")`) gives a pagination its own parameter
(`members_page`) and its links their own ids (`members-page-2`), as it does for the
[table's headers](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md#two-tables-on-one-page).

### Written by hand

With content of its own, `<sl:pagination>` is the `nav` around a pagination of parts, as in shadcn/ui:

**Example: Written by hand.** The parts, as in shadcn/ui's example.

```html
<sl:pagination aria-label="Invoice pages">
  <sl:pagination-content>
    <sl:pagination-item>
      <sl:pagination-previous href="#"/>
    </sl:pagination-item>
    <sl:pagination-item>
      <sl:pagination-link href="#">1</sl:pagination-link>
    </sl:pagination-item>
    <sl:pagination-item>
      <sl:pagination-link href="#" active>2</sl:pagination-link>
    </sl:pagination-item>
    <sl:pagination-item>
      <sl:pagination-link href="#">3</sl:pagination-link>
    </sl:pagination-item>
    <sl:pagination-item>
      <sl:pagination-ellipsis/>
    </sl:pagination-item>
    <sl:pagination-item>
      <sl:pagination-next href="#"/>
    </sl:pagination-item>
  </sl:pagination-content>
</sl:pagination>
```

`sl:pagination-link` takes `active` for the page shown now and `disabled` for nowhere to go; `sl:pagination-previous`
and `sl:pagination-next` take `disabled`, and content of their own replaces their text.

### Summary

`<sl:pagination-summary>` says which rows the page shows, or with `format="page"` which page it is:

**Example: Summary.**

```html
<sl:pagination-summary th:page="${people}"/>
```

**Example: Summary as the page number.**

```html
<sl:pagination-summary th:page="${people}" format="page"/>
```

A `Slice` has no total, so it reads "11–20" or "Page 2". The words are messages, so your `messages.properties` rewords
or translates them; the numbers are formatted for the locale ("1,001–1,010 of 12,345").

### Rows per page

`<sl:pagination-size>` is a label and a [dropdown menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/dropdown-menu.md) of sizes, as in shadcn/ui's data table:

**Example: Rows per page.** In a request for /people?sort=name,asc&page=3&size=20. Each size keeps the sort and starts on the first page.

```html
<sl:pagination-size th:page="${people}"/>
```

Each size is a link to the same request with that size, every other parameter kept except the page number, so the list
starts on its first page. It works without JavaScript: the menu is a popover. `sizes="10,20,50"` is the default; a size
the page has that is not in the list is added to it, so the menu always shows a checked one. Limit what the controller
accepts with `spring.data.web.pageable.max-page-size`.

### A table footer

Summary, size and pagination are separate, so you lay out the footer. shadcn/ui's data table puts the summary at the
start and the controls at the end:

```html
<div class="table-footer">
  <sl:pagination-summary th:page="${people}"/>
  <div class="table-footer-controls">
    <sl:pagination-size th:page="${people}"/>
    <sl:pagination th:page="${people}"/>
  </div>
</div>
```

```css
.table-footer { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; }
.table-footer-controls { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 1.5rem; }
/* The pagination centres itself across the full width by default. */
.table-footer .pagination { inline-size: auto; margin: 0; }
```

Sample-01's `/people` page does this.

### Focus after an htmx swap

Every link has an id: `page-previous`, `page-next` and `page-<number>` (prefixed with the qualifier). When htmx replaces
the list and its pagination, it gives the focus back to the element with the id that had it, so after Next the focus is
on the new Next. The size menu's button is `page-size-trigger`: the menu gives the focus back to it before the chosen
link is followed. [Tables with htmx](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tables-htmx.md) shows the whole page.

### Accessibility

- The `nav` is named "Pagination" (`sl.pagination.label`); an `aria-label` of your own replaces it, which two
  paginations on one page need.
- Previous and Next are named "Go to previous page" and "Go to next page". On a narrow screen only their chevron shows.
- The ellipsis reads "More pages", where shadcn/ui hides it from screen readers: a list item that says nothing is
  harder to follow.
- The size menu's button reads "Rows per page" followed by the size.

### Messages

| Key | English |
| --- | --- |
| `sl.pagination.label` | Pagination |
| `sl.pagination.previous`, `sl.pagination.previous.label` | Previous, Go to previous page |
| `sl.pagination.next`, `sl.pagination.next.label` | Next, Go to next page |
| `sl.pagination.more` | More pages |
| `sl.pagination.summary` | `{0}–{1} of {2}` |
| `sl.pagination.summary.slice` | `{0}–{1}` |
| `sl.pagination.summary.empty` | 0 of 0 |
| `sl.pagination.summary.page`, `sl.pagination.summary.page.slice` | `Page {0} of {1}`, `Page {0}` |
| `sl.pagination-size.label` | Rows per page |

### Left out

First and last page buttons (shadcn's dashboard has them; the first and the last page are always among the numbers),
a field to type a page number, and paging in the browser.

### Attributes

#### sl:pagination

Attributes of `<sl:pagination>`: Links to the other pages of a list, in a `nav`. Given the Spring Data `Page` it shows (`th:page="${people}"`) and no content of its own, it renders them all: Previous, the first and the last page, the current page with `siblings` on each side, an ellipsis for the pages left out, and Next. Every link keeps the request's other parameters (sort, size, filters) and has a stable id, so htmx can give the focus back after a swap. A `Slice`, which does not know how many pages there are, gets Previous and Next only. Without Spring Data, pass `current` and `total` instead. With content of its own it is the frame for a hand-written pagination of `sl:pagination-content`, `-item`, `-link`, `-previous`, `-next` and `-ellipsis`, as in shadcn/ui.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `th:page` | *object* | — | The Spring Data `Page` or `Slice` shown now. |
| `current` | *number* | — | Without a `page`: the page shown now, counting from 1. |
| `total` | *number* | — | Without a `page`: the number of pages. |
| `siblings` | *number* | `1` | How many pages to show on each side of the current one. |
| `qualifier` | *string* | — | The `@Qualifier` of the controller's `Pageable`, for a second list on the page: its links use `members_page` instead of `page`, and their ids start with `members-`. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:page="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:pagination-content

Attributes of `<sl:pagination-content>`: The list (`ul`) of a hand-written `sl:pagination`, holding `sl:pagination-item`s.

`sl:pagination-content` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:pagination-item

Attributes of `<sl:pagination-item>`: One entry (`li`) of a `sl:pagination-content`: holds a link, Previous, Next or an ellipsis.

`sl:pagination-item` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:pagination-link

Attributes of `<sl:pagination-link>`: A link to one page, drawn as a ghost button, or an outline one for the page shown now (`active`). Give it an `href` or `th:href`, and the page number as content.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `active` | *boolean* | — | Whether it is the page shown now: `aria-current="page"` and the outline look. |
| `size` | `xs`, `sm`, `default`, `lg`, `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`, `icon-lg` | `icon` | Size of the link, as on `sl:button`: square by default, for a number. |
| `disabled` | *boolean* | — | There is nowhere to go: the link loses its `href`, gets `aria-disabled` and leaves the tab order, as a disabled `sl:button as="a"`. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:active="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:pagination-previous

Attributes of `<sl:pagination-previous>`: The link to the previous page: a `sl:pagination-link` with a chevron and the text "Previous" (the message `sl.pagination.previous`), which content of its own replaces. Its name is "Go to previous page" (`sl.pagination.previous.label`); an `aria-label` replaces it. On a narrow screen only the chevron shows.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | *boolean* | — | There is no previous page: the link loses its `href`, gets `aria-disabled` and leaves the tab order. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:disabled="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:pagination-next

Attributes of `<sl:pagination-next>`: The link to the next page: a `sl:pagination-link` with a chevron and the text "Next" (the message `sl.pagination.next`), which content of its own replaces. Its name is "Go to next page" (`sl.pagination.next.label`); an `aria-label` replaces it. On a narrow screen only the chevron shows.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disabled` | *boolean* | — | There is no next page: the link loses its `href`, gets `aria-disabled` and leaves the tab order. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:disabled="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:pagination-ellipsis

Attributes of `<sl:pagination-ellipsis>`: Stands for the pages a `sl:pagination` leaves out: an ellipsis, read as "More pages" (the message `sl.pagination.more`).

`sl:pagination-ellipsis` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:pagination-summary

Attributes of `<sl:pagination-summary>`: Where the page is in the results, as text: "11–20 of 270", or with `format="page"` "Page 2 of 27". Takes the Spring Data `Page` shown now (`th:page`); for a `Slice`, which does not know the total, "11–20" or "Page 2". The words are messages (`sl.pagination.summary*`), so an application rewords or translates them; numbers are formatted for the locale.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `th:page` | *object* | — | The Spring Data `Page` or `Slice` shown now. |
| `format` | `range`, `page` | `range` | `range`: the rows shown and the total. `page`: the page number and the number of pages. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:page="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:pagination-size

Attributes of `<sl:pagination-size>`: "Rows per page" and a menu of page sizes, as in shadcn/ui's data table. The sizes are `sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item` links: each asks for the same request with that size, every other parameter kept except the page number, so the list starts on the first page. It works without JavaScript (the menu is a popover). Takes the Spring Data `Page` shown now, whose size is the checked one; a size the page has but `sizes` does not list is added. The label is the message `sl.pagination-size.label`. Attributes go to the wrapper.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `th:page` | *object* | — | The Spring Data `Page` or `Slice` shown now. |
| `sizes` | *string* | `10,20,50` | The sizes to choose from, separated by commas. |
| `qualifier` | *string* | — | The `@Qualifier` of the controller's `Pageable`, for a second list on the page: its links use `members_size` instead of `size`. |
| `id` | *string* | — | The menu's id; its button gets `-trigger` added, its label `-label`. `page-size` when not set, prefixed with the qualifier (`members-page-size`). |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:page="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

---

## Query params

> Hidden inputs that keep a table's order, page size and filters when a search form is sent.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/query-params/

**Example: Query params.** In a request for /people?q=ada&sort=email,desc&size=50&page=2. Sending the form asks for /people?q=…&sort=email,desc&size=50: the order and the size stay, the page starts again at the first.

```html
<form action="/people" method="get">
  <sl:label for="query-params-q">Search people</sl:label>
  <sl:input type="search" id="query-params-q" name="q" th:value="${param.q}" placeholder="Name or email"/>
  <sl:query-params except="q"/>
</form>
```

### Searching a sorted table

A search above a [table](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md) is a `GET` form: sending it asks for the same page with `?q=...`, which the
controller filters on. A browser sends only the form's own fields, so on its own the form would forget the table's
order and page size. `<sl:query-params>` copies the current request's other parameters into the form as hidden inputs:

```html
<form th:action="@{/people}" method="get" role="search">
  <sl:input type="search" name="q" th:value="${param.q}" aria-label="Search people"/>
  <sl:query-params except="q"/>
</form>
```

In a request for `/people?q=ada&sort=email,desc&size=50&page=2`, that renders:

```html
<form action="/people" method="get" role="search">
  <input class="input" type="search" name="q" value="ada" aria-label="Search people">
  <input type="hidden" name="sort" value="email,desc">
  <input type="hidden" name="size" value="50">
</form>
```

and searching for "grace" asks for `/people?q=grace&sort=email,desc&size=50`.

- `except` names the form's own fields, separated by commas (`except="q,status"`). Without it, `q` would be sent twice:
  the field's new value and the hidden copy of the old one.
- The page number is always left out, so a new search starts on the first page. It is the page parameter your
  `Pageable` reads (`spring.data.web.pageable.*`, see [parameter names](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md#parameter-names)); with
  `qualifier="members"` it is `members_page`, for the [second table](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/table.md#two-tables-on-one-page) on a page.
- A repeated parameter stays repeated, in its order: `?sort=name,desc&sort=email` gives two `sort` inputs, as Spring
  Data's `Sort` reads them.
- Values are decoded once (`?q=ada%20l%C3%A9` gives `value="ada lé"`) and escaped like any other attribute value, so a
  parameter cannot add markup.

The controller needs nothing for it: the `Pageable` reads `sort` and `size` as it does for the table's links.

```java
@GetMapping("/people")
String people(@RequestParam(required = false) String q, @PageableDefault(sort = "name") Pageable pageable,
    Model model) {
  Page<Person> people = q == null || q.isBlank()
      ? personRepository.findAll(pageable)
      : personRepository.findByNameContainingIgnoreCaseOrEmailContainingIgnoreCase(q, q, pageable);
  model.addAttribute("people", people);
  return "people";
}
```

The links of the table's headers, its [pagination](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/pagination.md) and the rows-per-page menu keep `q` in the same
way, as they are built from the request too.

### Outside the form

Other attributes go to every hidden input. With `form`, the inputs belong to a form elsewhere on the page. The
[live search with htmx](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/guides/tables-htmx.md) uses this to put them next to the table, so they are swapped with it
and follow the order of the table they came with:

```html
<form id="people-search" ...>...</form>
<div id="people-results">
  <sl:query-params except="q" form="people-search"/>
  <sl:table th:page="${people}">...</sl:table>
</div>
```

### Attributes

Attributes of `<sl:query-params>`: Hidden inputs that copy the current request's query parameters into a `GET` form, so sending a search keeps the table's order, page size and other filters. Name the form's own fields in `except`, or they are sent twice. The page number is always left out, so a new search starts on the first page. Values are decoded once and escaped like any other attribute; a repeated parameter (several `sort` values) stays repeated. Renders no element of its own. Other attributes go to every input: `form="search"` ties them to a form elsewhere on the page.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `except` | *string* | — | The parameters not to copy, separated by commas: the fields the form has itself (`q`, `q,status`). |
