Holds an `sl:attachment-media`, an `sl:attachment-content` (title and description), optional `sl:attachment-actions` and an optional `sl:attachment-trigger` that makes the whole card open a link or a dialog. Purely presentational: the server renders its state. Say the state in the description too ("Uploading · 64%", "Upload failed"), so it is not told by colour alone.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `idle`, `uploading`, `processing`, `error`, `done` | `done` | Where the file is in its upload: `idle` (picked, not sent yet) draws a dashed border, `uploading` and `processing` shimmer the title and mark the attachment busy (`aria-busy`), `error` turns it destructive. `done` is a file that is there. |
| `size` | `default`, `sm`, `xs` | `default` | Size of the attachment. |
| `orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | `horizontal` | `vertical` puts the media above the content, for an image. |
| `full-width` | *boolean* | — | Fill the width of the container, for a list of attachments (shadcn's `w-full` class). Without it the attachment is as wide as its content. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:state="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:attachment-media

Attributes of `<sl:attachment-media>`: The icon or image of an `sl:attachment`: an icon (or an `sl:spinner` while it uploads) on a muted square, or an `&lt;img&gt;` that fills it.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `icon`, `image` | `icon` | `icon` centres an icon on a muted square; `image` crops an `&lt;img&gt;` to fill the square, dimmed while the attachment uploads, is processed or failed. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:variant="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:attachment-content

Attributes of `<sl:attachment-content>`: The text of an `sl:attachment`: its `sl:attachment-title` and `sl:attachment-description`. Takes the space the media and the actions leave.

`sl:attachment-content` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:attachment-title

Attributes of `<sl:attachment-title>`: The name of an attachment, usually its file name, in `sl:attachment-content`. Cut off with an ellipsis when it does not fit; shimmers while the attachment uploads or is processed, unless the user asks for reduced motion.

`sl:attachment-title` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:attachment-description

Attributes of `<sl:attachment-description>`: What else to know about an attachment, below its title: the file type and size, or its state ("Uploading · 64%", "Upload failed. Try again."). Cut off with an ellipsis when it does not fit.

`sl:attachment-description` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:attachment-actions

Attributes of `<sl:attachment-actions>`: The `sl:attachment-action`s of an attachment, at its end; in a vertical attachment, over the top corner of the media. They sit above an `sl:attachment-trigger`, so they stay clickable.

`sl:attachment-actions` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:attachment-action

Attributes of `<sl:attachment-action>`: A button in `sl:attachment-actions`, to remove, retry or download the file: a `sl:button`, ghost and an extra small icon by default. Give it an `aria-label` that names the file ("Remove report.pdf"). Any other attribute passes through to the `sl:button` (`href`, `type`, `disabled`, `hx-*`).

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `default`, `outline`, `ghost`, `destructive`, `secondary`, `link` | `ghost` | Visual style of the button, as on `sl:button`. |
| `size` | `xs`, `sm`, `default`, `lg`, `icon`, `icon-xs`, `icon-sm`, `icon-lg` | `icon-xs` | Size of the button, as on `sl:button`. The `icon` sizes are square, for a button that holds only an icon, and need an `aria-label`. |
| `as` | `button`, `a` | `button` | Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`) to download or open the file. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:variant="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is required when `size` is `icon` or `icon-xs` or `icon-sm` or `icon-lg`; rendering fails without one.

#### sl:attachment-trigger

Attributes of `<sl:attachment-trigger>`: Makes a whole `sl:attachment` clickable: a button (to open an `sl:dialog` with `commandfor` and `command="show-modal"`) or, with `as="a"`, a link that covers the card behind its actions. It has no text of its own, so it needs an `aria-label` that says what it does ("Open report.pdf"). Put it last in the attachment.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | `button`, `a` | `button` | Element to render: a `button`, or an anchor (`a`) to open the file. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:as="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended. An `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` is required; rendering fails without one.

#### sl:attachment-group

Attributes of `<sl:attachment-group>`: A row of `sl:attachment`s that scrolls sideways when they do not fit, snapping to each attachment, its edges fading out. Keyboard users reach attachments off screen by tabbing to their actions or triggers; for attachments without any, give the group a `label`.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | *string* | — | Accessible name of the group. With it the group is a named group (`role="group"`) that takes keyboard focus, so the arrow keys scroll it: for a row of attachments that have no actions or trigger. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:label="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

---

## Badge

> A small label for a status, a count or a category.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/badge/

**Example: Badge.**

```html
<sl:badge>New</sl:badge>
```

### Variants

The same variants as the [button](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/button.md).

**Example: Variants.**

```html
<sl:badge>Default</sl:badge>
<sl:badge variant="secondary">Secondary</sl:badge>
<sl:badge variant="destructive">Destructive</sl:badge>
<sl:badge variant="outline">Outline</sl:badge>
<sl:badge variant="ghost">Ghost</sl:badge>
<sl:badge variant="link">Link</sl:badge>
```

### With an icon

Put an [`<sl:icon>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/icon.md) in the `icon-start` or `icon-end` slot. It takes the badge's colour and a 12 pixel size.

**Example: With an icon.**

```html
<sl:badge variant="secondary">
  <sl:slot name="icon-start"><sl:icon name="badge-check"/></sl:slot>
  Verified
</sl:badge>
<sl:badge variant="outline">
  Details
  <sl:slot name="icon-end"><sl:icon name="arrow-right"/></sl:slot>
</sl:badge>
```

### As a link

`as="a"` renders an anchor, for a badge that filters a list or opens a detail page. Only a linked badge reacts to hover
and shows a focus ring; a plain badge is not interactive, so it does not pretend to be.

**Example: As a link.** Only a linked badge changes on hover and takes keyboard focus.

```html
<sl:badge as="a" href="/orders?status=open">Open</sl:badge>
<sl:badge as="a" href="/orders?status=late" variant="destructive">Late</sl:badge>
<sl:badge as="a" href="/orders" variant="outline">
  All orders
  <sl:slot name="icon-end"><sl:icon name="arrow-up-right"/></sl:slot>
</sl:badge>
```

A badge is text, so a screen reader reads it where it stands. When a bare number or a single word would not make sense
out of context, write the context into the text, or next to the badge.

### Props from expressions

**Example: Props from an expression.**

```html
<sl:badge th:variant="${order.late ? 'destructive' : 'secondary'}"
          th:text="${order.status}">Open</sl:badge>
```

### Everything else passes through

**Example: Pass-through attributes.** Anything that is not a prop lands on the rendered element; class is appended.

```html
<sl:badge variant="outline" class="app-wide" id="order-status" data-testid="status">Shipped</sl:badge>
```

### Attributes

Attributes of `<sl:badge>`: A small label for a status, a count or a category; with `as="a"`, a link that looks the same. Every attribute that is not a prop passes through; `class` is appended to `badge`.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `default`, `secondary`, `destructive`, `outline`, `ghost`, `link` | `default` | Visual style of the badge. |
| `as` | `span`, `a` | `span` | Element to render: a `span`, or an anchor (`a`) for a badge that links somewhere. Only a linked badge reacts to hover. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:variant="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

---

## Avatar

> A picture of a person, with initials when there is no picture.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/avatar/

**Example: Avatar.**

```html
<sl:avatar label="shadcn">
  <sl:avatar-image th:src="@{/users/{id}/photo(id=${user.id})}"/>
  <sl:avatar-fallback>CN</sl:avatar-fallback>
</sl:avatar>
```

### Image and fallback

Write both parts, as in shadcn/ui: `<sl:avatar-image>` with the picture's `src` or `th:src`, and
`<sl:avatar-fallback>` with what to show without one, usually initials or an [`<sl:icon>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/icon.md). The avatar shows
the fallback when the image has no `src` or an empty one. A `th:src` whose value is null renders an empty `src`, so a
user without a photo needs no `th:if`:

**Example: Fallback.** A user without a photo gets their initials; th:src with a null value renders an empty src, which shows the fallback.

```html
<sl:avatar label="Jane Doe">
  <sl:avatar-image th:src="${user.photoUrl}"/>
  <sl:avatar-fallback>JD</sl:avatar-fallback>
</sl:avatar>
<sl:avatar label="Unknown user">
  <sl:avatar-fallback><sl:icon name="user"/></sl:avatar-fallback>
</sl:avatar>
```

Both parts are always rendered, and the stylesheet decides which one shows. The hidden one is also hidden from
assistive technology. The image lies over the fallback at the same size, so nothing moves when one replaces the other.

### A photo that fails to load

A photo URL that fails to load shows the fallback too: a 404, a URL your Content-Security-Policy's `img-src` blocks, a
file that is no image, or no network. So does a photo that is still loading, as in shadcn/ui; the picture replaces the
fallback once it is there.

**Example: Broken image.** A photo URL that fails to load (a 404, a URL the Content-Security-Policy blocks, offline) shows the fallback, as does one that is still loading.

```html
<sl:avatar label="Grace Hopper">
  <sl:avatar-image th:src="@{/users/{id}/photo(id=${user.id})}"/>
  <sl:avatar-fallback>GH</sl:avatar-fallback>
</sl:avatar>
```

Shadleaf's script marks each avatar image with `data-status="loaded"` when its picture has loaded, or
`data-status="error"`, and the stylesheet only shows an image that is marked loaded. So a broken image never shows, not
even for a moment before the script runs. The script also marks images htmx swaps in, and an image whose `src` changes
later (htmx swapping the attribute, or a script of yours): the fallback shows while the new picture loads.

Your own CSS can use the mark, for instance to fade the picture in:

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
  .avatar-image[data-status='loaded'] {
    animation: avatar-fade-in 150ms;
  }
}

@keyframes avatar-fade-in {
  from { opacity: 0; }
}
```

#### Without the script

- **Without JavaScript**, nothing marks the images, so they lie over the fallback as plain images: a picture that loads
  covers it. One that fails shows the fallback through it in Firefox, which draws nothing for a broken image with an
  empty `alt`; Chromium draws its broken-image icon over it.
- **With JavaScript but without Shadleaf's script** (your policy blocks it, say), every avatar shows its fallback.

The script is part of the one in the `assets` fragment, whatever `shadleaf.assets.alpine` is: it is not an Alpine
component, and works without Alpine on the page. One listener on the document handles every avatar, so a long list of
them costs nothing extra.

### Sizes

**Example: Sizes.**

```html
<sl:avatar size="sm" label="Jane Doe"><sl:avatar-fallback>JD</sl:avatar-fallback></sl:avatar>
<sl:avatar label="Jane Doe"><sl:avatar-fallback>JD</sl:avatar-fallback></sl:avatar>
<sl:avatar size="lg" label="Jane Doe"><sl:avatar-fallback>JD</sl:avatar-fallback></sl:avatar>
```

### Naming the avatar

An avatar usually sits next to the person's name, so it is decorative by default and hidden from assistive technology.
When there is no name next to it, give it a `label`: it is then announced as an image with that name, whichever part
shows. `aria-labelledby`, pointing at a name elsewhere on the page, works too.

**Example: Next to a name.** Without a label the avatar is decorative; the name beside it is what a screen reader reads.

```html
<sl:avatar><sl:avatar-fallback>JD</sl:avatar-fallback></sl:avatar>
<span>Jane Doe</span>
```

### Left out

- **A delay before the fallback shows** (Radix's `delayMs`): the fallback shows at once while a photo loads. A photo
  from the browser's cache is there before the first paint, so it does not flash.
- **A loading status event** (Radix's `onLoadingStatusChange`): read `data-status` on the image instead.

### Attributes

#### sl:avatar

Attributes of `<sl:avatar>`: A picture of a person: an `sl:avatar-image`, and an `sl:avatar-fallback` (initials) shown instead while the image has no `src`, is loading or fails to load. Decorative unless it has a `label`, as an avatar usually sits next to the person's name.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `sm`, `default`, `lg` | `default` | Size of the avatar. |
| `label` | *string* | — | The person's name, for an avatar with no name next to it. It is then announced as an image with that name; without it the avatar is hidden from assistive technology. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:size="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

#### sl:avatar-image

Attributes of `<sl:avatar-image>`: The picture inside `sl:avatar`. Pass `src` or `th:src`; when it is empty or null, while the picture loads, and when it fails to load (marked by Shadleaf's script), the image is hidden and the `sl:avatar-fallback` shows instead. The avatar's `label` names it, so the image itself has an empty `alt`.

`sl:avatar-image` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:avatar-fallback

Attributes of `<sl:avatar-fallback>`: What `sl:avatar` shows when its image has no `src`, while it loads and when it fails to load: usually the person's initials, or an `sl:icon`.

`sl:avatar-fallback` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

---

## Icon

> Inline SVG icons from lucide, or your own.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/icon/

`<sl:icon>` inlines the SVG of a [lucide](https://lucide.dev) icon into the page: no sprite, no extra request, and it
works inside htmx swaps. It draws in `currentColor`, so it takes the colour of the text around it. An unknown name
fails with the closest known ones.

**Example: Icon.**

```html
<sl:icon name="leaf"/>
<sl:icon name="trash"/>
<sl:icon name="settings"/>
```

### Size and stroke width

**Example: Sizes.**

```html
<sl:icon name="leaf" size="16"/>
<sl:icon name="leaf"/>
<sl:icon name="leaf" size="32"/>
```
**Example: Stroke width.**

```html
<sl:icon name="leaf" stroke-width="1"/>
<sl:icon name="leaf"/>
<sl:icon name="leaf" stroke-width="3"/>
```

### Decorative or meaningful

Without a `label` an icon is decorative: it renders `aria-hidden="true"`, which is right next to text or inside a
labelled button. With a `label` it is announced as an image with that name.

**Example: A meaningful icon.** With a label the icon is announced as an image; without one it is hidden from assistive technology.

```html
<sl:icon name="circle-alert" label="Warning"/>
```

### Your own icons

Register an `IconSource` bean. Sources are asked in `@Order`, before the bundled lucide icons, so your icons can also
replace lucide's:

```java
@Bean
IconSource applicationIcons() {
  // reads src/main/resources/icons/<name>.svg
  return IconSource.classpathDirectory("icons/");
}
```

### Attributes

Attributes of `<sl:icon>`: Inlines the SVG of an icon: the bundled lucide icons, or the application's own through an `IconSource` bean. An unknown name fails with the closest known ones.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | *string* | — | Name of the icon, e.g. `trash`. Lucide's names and aliases, plus any icons the application registers. |
| `size` | *number* | — | Width and height in pixels. Without it the icon is 24 pixels, or sized by the surrounding component (16 pixels inside a button). |
| `stroke-width` | *number* | — | Stroke width, overriding the icon's own (2 for lucide). |
| `label` | *string* | — | Accessible name for an icon that carries meaning on its own. Without it the icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:name="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

---

## Kbd

> A key on the keyboard, or a combination of keys.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/kbd/

**Example: Kbd.**

```html
<sl:kbd>Esc</sl:kbd>
<sl:kbd>Enter</sl:kbd>
<sl:kbd>/</sl:kbd>
```

`<sl:kbd>` renders HTML's own `<kbd>` element, so it fits in running text.

**Example: In a sentence.**

```html
<p>Press <sl:kbd>/</sl:kbd> to search.</p>
```

### Key combinations

Put the keys pressed together in `<sl:kbd-group>`. It is an outer `<kbd>`, which is how HTML marks up a combination.
Text between the keys, such as `+`, is up to you.

**Example: A key combination.**

```html
<sl:kbd-group>
  <sl:kbd>Ctrl</sl:kbd>
  <sl:kbd>Shift</sl:kbd>
  <sl:kbd>P</sl:kbd>
</sl:kbd-group>
<sl:kbd-group><sl:kbd>Ctrl</sl:kbd>+<sl:kbd>K</sl:kbd></sl:kbd-group>
```

### Icons

A key can hold an [`<sl:icon>`](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/icon.md). Give the icon a `label`, as a screen reader has no text to read otherwise.
An `aria-label` on the key itself would not do: `<kbd>` has no role that takes a name.

Lucide has icons for the usual keys, so you never need to type a symbol: `command`, `option`, `arrow-big-up` (Shift),
`corner-down-left` (Enter), `delete` (Backspace), `arrow-up` / `arrow-down` / `arrow-left` / `arrow-right`, and
`space`.

**Example: With an icon.** An icon on its own has no text, so give the key a name.

```html
<sl:kbd-group>
  <sl:kbd><sl:icon name="command" label="Command"/></sl:kbd>
  <sl:kbd>K</sl:kbd>
</sl:kbd-group>
```

### In a button

A key can sit next to a button's label, to show its shortcut. Hide the key from screen readers with
`aria-hidden="true"`, or it becomes part of the button's name ("Accept Enter"), and name the shortcut in
`aria-keyshortcuts` on the button instead. An icon in a hidden key needs no `label`. `aria-keyshortcuts` only
announces the shortcut: listening for the key is up to your own script.

**Example: In a button.** The shortcut goes in aria-keyshortcuts; the key itself is hidden from screen readers.

```html
<sl:button aria-keyshortcuts="Enter">
  Accept <sl:kbd aria-hidden="true"><sl:icon name="corner-down-left"/></sl:kbd>
</sl:button>
<sl:button variant="outline" aria-keyshortcuts="Escape">
  Cancel <sl:kbd aria-hidden="true">Esc</sl:kbd>
</sl:button>
```

### Attributes

#### sl:kbd

Attributes of `<sl:kbd>`: A key on the keyboard, as text (`Ctrl`) or an `sl:icon`. Several keys pressed together go in an `sl:kbd-group`.

`sl:kbd` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

#### sl:kbd-group

Attributes of `<sl:kbd-group>`: A key combination: `sl:kbd` elements, with any text between them (such as `+`). HTML nests the keys of a combination in an outer `kbd`, as this does.

`sl:kbd-group` declares no props; every attribute passes through.

---

## Separator

> A thin line between content.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/separator/

**Example: Separator.**

```html
<sl:separator/>
```

### Vertical

`orientation="vertical"` draws a vertical line that stretches to the height of the row it is in. Put it in a flex
container, such as a toolbar or a row of links.

**Example: Vertical.** A vertical separator stretches to the height of the flex row it is in.

```html
<sl:button as="a" href="/blog" variant="link">Blog</sl:button>
<sl:separator orientation="vertical"/>
<sl:button as="a" href="/docs" variant="link">Docs</sl:button>
<sl:separator orientation="vertical"/>
<sl:button as="a" href="/source" variant="link">Source</sl:button>
```

### Decorative or announced

A separator is decorative by default, as in shadcn/ui: it only draws a line and is hidden from assistive technology
(`role="none"`). When the line divides the content into groups a screen reader user should know about, write
`decorative="false"`. It is then announced as a separator (`role="separator"`, with `aria-orientation` when
vertical).

**Example: Announced.** decorative="false" makes it a separator for assistive technology too.

```html
<sl:separator decorative="false"/>
```

### Attributes

Attributes of `<sl:separator>`: A thin line between content. A vertical one stretches to the height of the row it is in, so it needs a flex container.

| Attribute | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `orientation` | `horizontal`, `vertical` | `horizontal` | Direction of the line. |
| `decorative` | *boolean* | `true` | Hide the line from assistive technology, as most separators only draw a line. With `decorative="false"` it is announced as a separator, for one that divides content into groups. |

Every prop can also be set from an expression: `th:orientation="${...}"`. Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and `class` is appended.

---

## Layouts

> Whole layout files to copy into an application, each with a page that uses it and the CSS around it, after shadcn/ui's sidebar blocks.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/

A layout is the frame every page of an application shares: the navigation, the page's header, the skip link, and the
places where dialogs and toasts appear. In Thymeleaf it is one template, `templates/layout/main.html`, whose fragment
every page fills in with its title and content. The layouts here are built from Shadleaf's
[application shell](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md) components, most of them after one of
[shadcn/ui's sidebar blocks](https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks/sidebar), and each one has what
[every layout needs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#what-every-layout-needs).

### What a layout page holds

- **A preview**, at a desktop's width and, with the Phone switch, at a phone's. The navigation is one element for
  both: beside the page (or in the header) from 768 px, a panel the menu button opens below that. The preview works:
  open the menus, collapse the sidebar, open the panel.
- **The layout**: the whole layout file, head included, ready to copy.
- **A page**: a page that uses it. It passes its title, its content and, where the layout has a breadcrumb, the
  breadcrumb's levels, as fragments of itself (`th:ref`), so nothing is rendered where it stands.
- **The CSS**: what the layout needs of the application's own CSS. Shadleaf's CSS styles the components, not the page
  around them, and has no utility classes, so the page's padding, a logo's square or a border below the header are
  yours. It is plain CSS, without Tailwind, on Shadleaf's colour tokens, so it follows the skin and the dark theme.

### Using one

Copy the layout file to `src/main/resources/templates/layout/main.html` and its CSS into your stylesheet, then
replace the example navigation with your own pages. Mark the current page with `#slNav.current`, which reads the
request, so no controller has to tell the layout which page it is. The template is yours from then on: Shadleaf
does not update it, and nothing in it is configuration. Which kind of layout suits an application, a sidebar or a
header, is on the [Application shell](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#which-one) page, with the htmx check a
controller needs when the layout boosts its links.

The first sample application uses a shorter [Collapses to icons](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/collapses-to-icons.md), the second
[Navigation in the header](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/header.md).

### The layouts

- [Grouped by section](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/grouped-by-section.md): A sidebar of sections, each a group of pages under its label, with a version switcher and a search field, as documentation has.
- [Collapsible sections](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/collapsible-sections.md): A sidebar of sections whose labels open and close them, with a version switcher and a search field, as documentation has.
- [Sub-menus](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/sub-menus.md): A sidebar of sections with their pages in sub-menus that are always open, as documentation has.
- [Floating, with sub-menus](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/floating-sub-menus.md): The sections and sub-menus of the Sub-menus layout in a floating sidebar, wider and with more room between the sections.
- [Collapsible sub-menus](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/collapsible-sub-menus.md): A sidebar of sections that open and close, each with its pages in a sub-menu, only the current page's section open.
- [Collapses to icons](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/collapses-to-icons.md): A team switcher, collapsible sections and projects beside the page, collapsing to a strip of icons on a desktop, with the page as a card and the signed-in user's menu at the bottom.
- [Inset with secondary navigation](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/inset-secondary-navigation.md): Sections that are pages of their own with a chevron for their sub-menus, projects, a secondary navigation and the user menu, beside the page as a card.
- [Sidebar and top bar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/top-bar.md): A sidebar that is always there on a desktop, with the pages, the user's teams and Settings, and a bar across the top with a search field, the notifications and the signed-in user's menu.
- [On the end](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/sidebar-end.md): A table of contents in a sidebar on the end of the line, the right in a left-to-right page, with the trigger at the end of the page's header.
- [Navigation in the header](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/header.md): For an application with a handful of pages, the pages as a row of links in the site header and the page as a card below it; on a phone the same navigation is a panel.

---

## Grouped by section

> A sidebar of sections, each a group of pages under its label, with a version switcher and a search field, as documentation has.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/grouped-by-section/

A sidebar for an application whose pages fall into a handful of sections, such as documentation: each section is a
[group](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md) whose label names it, with its pages below, so the whole structure is in view. At
the top, a version switcher (a [dropdown menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/dropdown-menu.md#opened-from-the-sidebar) opened from a
large menu button) and a search field. The page's header has the trigger and the
[breadcrumb](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/breadcrumb.md). On a desktop the trigger moves the sidebar out of view; on a phone it opens
the same sidebar as a panel. Switch the preview to Phone to see it.

**Example: Grouped by section.** A sidebar of sections, each a group of pages under its label, with a version switcher and a search field at the top, as in documentation. The trigger moves the sidebar out of view on a desktop and opens it as a panel on a phone.

For reference: the [shadcn/ui block](https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks/sidebar#sidebar-01) this layout is based on.

### The layout

The whole layout file. It has what [every layout needs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#what-every-layout-needs): the
theme script and Shadleaf's assets in the head, the skip link first, one `main` (`<sl:sidebar-inset>`), the page's
title, and the toaster. `#slNav.current` marks the current page from the request.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:fragment="layout(pageTitle, breadcrumb, content)">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title th:text="${pageTitle}">Page</title>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: theme-script}"></th:block>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: assets}"></th:block>
  <link rel="stylesheet" th:href="@{/css/application.css}">
</head>
<body>
<sl:skip-link/>
<sl:sidebar-provider>
  <sl:sidebar>
    <sl:sidebar-header>
      <sl:sidebar-menu>
        <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          <sl:dropdown-menu id="version-switcher">
            <sl:dropdown-menu-trigger as="sidebar-menu-button" size="lg">
              <sl:slot name="icon-start"><span class="app-logo"><sl:icon name="gallery-vertical-end"/></span></sl:slot>
              <strong>Documentation</strong>
              <small>v1.0.1</small>
              <sl:slot name="icon-end"><sl:icon name="chevrons-up-down"/></sl:slot>
            </sl:dropdown-menu-trigger>
            <sl:dropdown-menu-content>
              <sl:dropdown-menu-radio-group aria-label="Versions">
                <sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item as="a" th:href="@{/}" checked>v1.0.1</sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item>
                <sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item as="a" th:href="@{/1.1.0-alpha/}">v1.1.0-alpha</sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item>
                <sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item as="a" th:href="@{/2.0.0-beta1/}">v2.0.0-beta1</sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item>
              </sl:dropdown-menu-radio-group>
            </sl:dropdown-menu-content>
          </sl:dropdown-menu>
        </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
      </sl:sidebar-menu>
      <form class="docs-search" role="search" th:action="@{/search}">
        <sl:input type="search" name="q" placeholder="Search the docs..." aria-label="Search the docs"/>
        <sl:icon name="search"/>
      </form>
    </sl:sidebar-header>
    <sl:sidebar-content>
      <sl:sidebar-group id="nav-getting">
        <sl:sidebar-group-label>Getting Started</sl:sidebar-group-label>
        <sl:sidebar-group-content>
          <sl:sidebar-menu>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/getting-started/installation}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/getting-started/installation')}">Installation</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/getting-started/project-structure}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/getting-started/project-structure')}">Project Structure</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          </sl:sidebar-menu>
        </sl:sidebar-group-content>
      </sl:sidebar-group>
      <sl:sidebar-group id="nav-build">
        <sl:sidebar-group-label>Build Your Application</sl:sidebar-group-label>
        <sl:sidebar-group-content>
          <sl:sidebar-menu>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/routing}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/routing')}">Routing</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/data-fetching}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/data-fetching')}">Data Fetching</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/rendering}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/rendering')}">Rendering</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/caching}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/caching')}">Caching</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/styling}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/styling')}">Styling</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/optimizing}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/optimizing')}">Optimizing</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/configuring}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/configuring')}">Configuring</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/testing}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/testing')}">Testing</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/authentication}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/authentication')}">Authentication</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/deploying}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/deploying')}">Deploying</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/upgrading}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/upgrading')}">Upgrading</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build/examples}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/examples')}">Examples</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          </sl:sidebar-menu>
        </sl:sidebar-group-content>
      </sl:sidebar-group>
      <sl:sidebar-group id="nav-api">
        <sl:sidebar-group-label>API Reference</sl:sidebar-group-label>
        <sl:sidebar-group-content>
          <sl:sidebar-menu>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/api/components}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/api/components')}">Components</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/api/file-conventions}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/api/file-conventions')}">File Conventions</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/api/functions}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/api/functions')}">Functions</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/api/configuration-options}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/api/configuration-options')}">Configuration Options</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/api/cli}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/api/cli')}">CLI</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/api/edge-runtime}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/api/edge-runtime')}">Edge Runtime</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          </sl:sidebar-menu>

      </sl:sidebar-group>
      <sl:sidebar-group id="nav-architecture">
        <sl:sidebar-group-label>Architecture</sl:sidebar-group-label>
        <sl:sidebar-group-content>
          <sl:sidebar-menu>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/architecture/accessibility}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/architecture/accessibility')}">Accessibility</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/architecture/fast-refresh}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/architecture/fast-refresh')}">Fast Refresh</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/architecture/compiler}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/architecture/compiler')}">Compiler</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/architecture/supported-browsers}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/architecture/supported-browsers')}">Supported Browsers</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/architecture/bundler}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/architecture/bundler')}">Bundler</sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          </sl:sidebar-menu>
        </sl:sidebar-group-content>
      </sl:sidebar-group>
    </sl:sidebar-content>
  </sl:sidebar>
  <sl:sidebar-inset>
    <sl:site-header>
      <sl:sidebar-trigger/>
      <sl:separator orientation="vertical"/>
      <sl:breadcrumb>
        <sl:breadcrumb-list>
          <th:block th:replace="${breadcrumb}"></th:block>
        </sl:breadcrumb-list>
      </sl:breadcrumb>
    </sl:site-header>
    <div class="page">
      <h1 th:text="${pageTitle}"></h1>
      <div th:replace="${content}"></div>
    </div>
  </sl:sidebar-inset>
</sl:sidebar-provider>
<div id="modal-root"></div>
<sl:toaster>
  <sl:toast th:each="toast : ${toasts}" th:title="${toast.title}" th:description="${toast.description}"
            th:variant="${toast.variant}" th:duration="${toast.duration}"/>
</sl:toaster>
</body>
</html>
```

The versions are links, and the server checks the one being read (`checked`), so the switcher works without
JavaScript. Here the check is fixed in the markup; an application that serves several versions sets it with
`th:checked`. The search field is a plain `GET` form; Shadleaf has no search of its own.

### A page

A page passes its title, its breadcrumb's levels and its content. The levels are a `th:block` with `th:ref`, so
nothing of it is rendered where it stands; the layout puts them in its `<sl:breadcrumb-list>`.

```html
<html xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:replace="~{layout/main :: layout('Data Fetching', ~{::breadcrumb}, ~{::#page-content})}">
<body>
<th:block th:ref="breadcrumb">
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-link th:href="@{/build}">Build Your Application</sl:breadcrumb-link>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
  <sl:breadcrumb-separator/>
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-page>Data Fetching</sl:breadcrumb-page>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
</th:block>
<div id="page-content">
  ...
</div>
</body>
</html>
```

### The CSS

Shadleaf's CSS styles the components, not the page around them, and has no utility classes. The rest is the
application's CSS, here without Tailwind: the square behind the logo, the magnifier in the search field (the
`docs-search` class on the form) and its height, a border below the header, and the page's padding.

```css
/* The square behind the logo in the version switcher. */
.app-logo {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  inline-size: 2rem;
  block-size: 2rem;
  border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px);
  background: var(--sidebar-primary);
  color: var(--sidebar-primary-foreground);
}
.app-logo > svg { inline-size: 1rem; block-size: 1rem; }

/* The search field: a magnifier inside it, at the start. */
.docs-search { position: relative; }
.docs-search > .input {
  block-size: 2rem;
  padding-inline-start: 2rem;
  background: var(--background);
}
.docs-search > svg {
  position: absolute;
  inset-inline-start: 0.5rem;
  inset-block-start: 50%;
  translate: 0 -50%;
  inline-size: 1rem;
  block-size: 1rem;
  opacity: 0.5;
  pointer-events: none;
}

/* A border below the page's header, and the page's padding. */
.sidebar-inset > .site-header { border-block-end: 1px solid var(--border); }
.page { padding: 1rem; }
.page > h1 { margin-block-end: 1rem; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; }
```

## Collapsible sections

> A sidebar of sections whose labels open and close them, with a version switcher and a search field, as documentation has.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/collapsible-sections/

The [grouped layout](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/grouped-by-section.md) with sections that open and close: each section is a
[collapsible group](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md#collapsible-sections) whose label is what the user clicks, with a
chevron that turns when it opens. Every section starts open here; a long sidebar can open only the current page's
section with `th:open="${#slNav.current('/build')}"`. At the top, a version switcher and a search field. On a desktop
the trigger moves the sidebar out of view; on a phone it opens the same sidebar as a panel. Switch the preview to
Phone to see it.

**Example: Collapsible sections.** A sidebar of sections, each a group of pages under a label that opens and closes it, with a version switcher and a search field at the top. The trigger moves the sidebar out of view on a desktop and opens it as a panel on a phone.

For reference: the [shadcn/ui block](https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks/sidebar#sidebar-02) this layout is based on.

### The layout

The whole layout file. It has what [every layout needs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#what-every-layout-needs): the
theme script and Shadleaf's assets in the head, the skip link first, one `main` (`<sl:sidebar-inset>`), the page's
title, and the toaster. A section is the browser's `details` element, so it opens and closes without JavaScript, and
a closed one is still found by the browser's find in page.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:fragment="layout(pageTitle, breadcrumb, content)">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title th:text="${pageTitle}">Page</title>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: theme-script}"></th:block>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: assets}"></th:block>
  <link rel="stylesheet" th:href="@{/css/application.css}">
</head>
<body>
<sl:skip-link/>
<sl:sidebar-provider>
  <sl:sidebar>
    <sl:sidebar-header>
      <sl:sidebar-menu>
        <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          <sl:dropdown-menu id="version-switcher">
            <sl:dropdown-menu-trigger as="sidebar-menu-button" size="lg">
              <sl:slot name="icon-start"><span class="app-logo"><sl:icon name="gallery-vertical-end"/></span></sl:slot>
              <strong>Documentation</strong>
              <small>v1.0.1</small>
              <sl:slot name="icon-end"><sl:icon name="chevrons-up-down"/></sl:slot>
            </sl:dropdown-menu-trigger>
            <sl:dropdown-menu-content>
              <sl:dropdown-menu-radio-group aria-label="Versions">
                <sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item as="a" th:href="@{/}" checked>v1.0.1</sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item>
                <sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item as="a" th:href="@{/1.1.0-alpha/}">v1.1.0-alpha</sl:dropdown-menu-radio-item>

              </sl:dropdown-menu-radio-group>
            </sl:dropdown-menu-content>
          </sl:dropdown-menu>
        </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
      </sl:sidebar-menu>
      <form class="docs-search" role="search" th:action="@{/search}">
```

### A page

A page passes its title, its breadcrumb's levels and its content. The levels are a `th:block` with `th:ref`, so
nothing of it is rendered where it stands; the layout puts them in its `<sl:breadcrumb-list>`.

```html
<html xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:replace="~{layout/main :: layout('Data Fetching', ~{::breadcrumb}, ~{::#page-content})}">
<body>
<th:block th:ref="breadcrumb">
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-link th:href="@{/build}">Build Your Application</sl:breadcrumb-link>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
  <sl:breadcrumb-separator/>
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-page>Data Fetching</sl:breadcrumb-page>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
</th:block>
<div id="page-content">
  ...
</div>
</body>
</html>
```

### The CSS

Shadleaf's CSS styles the components, not the page around them, and has no utility classes. The rest is the
application's CSS, here without Tailwind: the square behind the logo, the magnifier in the search field, sections
without a gap between them and with labels in the links' size and colour (the `docs-sections` class on the
content), a border below the header, and the page's padding.

```css
/* The square behind the logo in the sidebar's header. */
.app-logo {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  inline-size: 2rem;
  block-size: 2rem;
  border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px);
  background: var(--sidebar-primary);
  color: var(--sidebar-primary-foreground);
}
.app-logo > svg { inline-size: 1rem; block-size: 1rem; }

/* The search field: a magnifier inside it, at the start. */
.docs-search { position: relative; }
.docs-search > .input {
  block-size: 2rem;
  padding-inline-start: 2rem;
  background: var(--background);
}
.docs-search > svg {
  position: absolute;
  inset-inline-start: 0.5rem;
  inset-block-start: 50%;
  translate: 0 -50%;
  inline-size: 1rem;
  block-size: 1rem;
  opacity: 0.5;
  pointer-events: none;
}

/* The sections close up, and their labels read as the links below them (shadcn's sidebar-02). */
.docs-sections { gap: 0; }
.docs-sections summary.sidebar-group-label:not(:hover) {
  font-size: 0.875rem;
  color: var(--sidebar-foreground);
}

/* A border below the page's header, and the page's padding. */
.sidebar-inset > .site-header { border-block-end: 1px solid var(--border); }
.page { padding: 1rem; }
.page > h1 { margin-block-end: 1rem; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; }
```

## Sub-menus

> A sidebar of sections with their pages in sub-menus that are always open, as documentation has.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/sub-menus/

A sidebar for an application whose pages fall into a handful of sections, such as documentation: each section is a
link of its own with its pages in a [sub-menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md#collapsible-groups) below it, always open, so
the whole structure is in view. The application's name and version are at the top. The page's header has the
trigger and the [breadcrumb](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/breadcrumb.md). On a desktop the trigger moves the sidebar out of view; on
a phone it opens the same sidebar as a panel. Switch the preview to Phone to see it.

**Example: Sub-menus.** A sidebar of sections, each with its pages in a sub-menu that is always open, as in documentation. The current page is a sub-button; the trigger moves the sidebar out of view on a desktop and opens it as a panel on a phone.

For reference: the [shadcn/ui block](https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks/sidebar#sidebar-03) this layout is based on.

The [floating variant](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/floating-sub-menus.md) has the same menus in a panel with a margin round it.

### The layout

The whole layout file. It has what [every layout needs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#what-every-layout-needs): the
theme script and Shadleaf's assets in the head, the skip link first, one `main` (`<sl:sidebar-inset>`), the page's
title, and the toaster. `#slNav.current` marks the current page from the request: the sections compare the exact path
(`true`), so a section is not marked as well when one of its pages is shown.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:fragment="layout(pageTitle, breadcrumb, content)">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title th:text="${pageTitle}">Page</title>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: theme-script}"></th:block>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: assets}"></th:block>
  <link rel="stylesheet" th:href="@{/css/application.css}">
</head>
<body>
<sl:skip-link/>
<sl:sidebar-provider>
  <sl:sidebar>
    <sl:sidebar-header>
      <sl:sidebar-menu>
        <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/}" size="lg">
            <sl:slot name="icon-start"><span class="app-logo"><sl:icon name="gallery-vertical-end"/></span></sl:slot>
            <strong>Documentation</strong>
            <small>v1.0.0</small>
          </sl:sidebar-menu-button>
        </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
      </sl:sidebar-menu>
    </sl:sidebar-header>
    <sl:sidebar-content>
      <sl:sidebar-group>
        <sl:sidebar-menu class="docs-nav">
          <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/getting-started}"
                                    th:active="${#slNav.current('/getting-started', true)}">
              Getting Started
            </sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-sub>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/getting-started/installation}"
                                            th:active="${#slNav.current('/getting-started/installation')}">
                  Installation
                </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/getting-started/project-structure}"
                                            th:active="${#slNav.current('/getting-started/project-structure')}">
                  Project Structure
                </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-sub>
          </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/build}"
                                    th:active="${#slNav.current('/build', true)}">
              Build Your Application
            </sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-sub>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/build/routing}"
                                            th:active="${#slNav.current('/build/routing')}">
                  Routing
                </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/build/data-fetching}"

            </sl:sidebar-menu-sub>
```

A page passes its title, its breadcrumb's levels and its content. The levels are a `th:block` with `th:ref`, so
nothing of it is rendered where it stands; the layout puts them in its `<sl:breadcrumb-list>`.


### The CSS

Shadleaf's CSS styles the components, not the page around them, and has no utility classes. The rest is the
application's CSS, here without Tailwind: the square behind the logo, the weight of the sections' links (the `docs-nav` class on the menu), a border below the header, and the page's padding.

```css
/* The square behind the logo in the sidebar's header. */
.app-logo {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  inline-size: 2rem;
  block-size: 2rem;
  border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px);
  background: var(--sidebar-primary);
  color: var(--sidebar-primary-foreground);

.app-logo > svg { inline-size: 1rem; block-size: 1rem; }

/* The sections' links in a medium weight, their pages' in the normal one. */
.docs-nav > .sidebar-menu-item > .sidebar-menu-button { font-weight: 500; }
```

## Floating, with sub-menus

> The sections and sub-menus of the Sub-menus layout in a floating sidebar, wider and with more room between the sections.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/floating-sub-menus/

The [Sub-menus](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/sub-menus.md) layout with `variant="floating"`: on a desktop the sidebar is a panel with a margin all
round, rounded corners (in the vega skin) and a shadow, instead of a column along the edge of the screen. The
application's CSS makes it wider (19 rem), puts more room between the sections and takes the line away from the
sub-menus. The page's header has no border. On a phone the panel is the same as for every
[variant](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md#variants).

**Example: Floating, with sub-menus.** The same sections and sub-menus in a floating sidebar: a panel with a margin all round, rounded and with a shadow, wider than the default, with more room between the sections and no line along the sub-menus.

For reference: the [shadcn/ui block](https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks/sidebar#sidebar-04) this layout is based on.

### The layout

The whole layout file, with what [every layout needs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#what-every-layout-needs). The
sub-menus have a class of their own, `docs-nav-sub`, for the CSS below.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:fragment="layout(pageTitle, breadcrumb, content)">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title th:text="${pageTitle}">Page</title>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: theme-script}"></th:block>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: assets}"></th:block>
  <link rel="stylesheet" th:href="@{/css/application.css}">
</head>
<body>
<sl:skip-link/>
<sl:sidebar-provider>
  <sl:sidebar variant="floating">
    <sl:sidebar-header>
      <sl:sidebar-menu>
```

### A page

A page passes its title, its breadcrumb's levels and its content, as for the [Sub-menus](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/sub-menus.md#a-page)
layout:

```html
<html xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:replace="~{layout/main :: layout('Data Fetching', ~{::breadcrumb}, ~{::#page-content})}">
<body>
<th:block th:ref="breadcrumb">
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-link th:href="@{/build}">Build Your Application</sl:breadcrumb-link>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
  <sl:breadcrumb-separator/>
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-page>Data Fetching</sl:breadcrumb-page>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
</th:block>
<div id="page-content">
  ...
</div>
</body>
</html>
```

### The CSS

The width is a token: `--sidebar-width` on `.sidebar-provider` replaces the skin's 16 rem, and the floating panel's
footprint follows it. Rules outside a cascade layer, as here, win over Shadleaf's, which are in one.

```css
/* The square behind the logo in the sidebar's header. */
.app-logo {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  inline-size: 2rem;
  block-size: 2rem;
  border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px);
  background: var(--sidebar-primary);
  color: var(--sidebar-primary-foreground);
}
.app-logo > svg { inline-size: 1rem; block-size: 1rem; }

/* A wider sidebar, more room between the sections, the sub-menus without their line. */
.sidebar-provider { --sidebar-width: 19rem; }
.docs-nav { gap: 0.5rem; }
.docs-nav > .sidebar-menu-item > .sidebar-menu-button { font-weight: 500; }
.docs-nav-sub { margin-inline: 0; border-inline-start: 0; padding-inline: 0.375rem; }

/* The page's padding: the header above it has its own. */
.page { padding: 0 1rem 1rem; }
.page > h1 { margin-block-end: 1rem; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; }
```

---

## Collapsible sub-menus

> A sidebar of sections that open and close, each with its pages in a sub-menu, only the current page's section open.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/collapsible-sub-menus/

The [sub-menus layout](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/sub-menus.md) for more pages than fit in view: every section is a
[collapsible item](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md#collapsible-groups) that opens and closes its sub-menu, and the server
opens only the section that holds the current page (`th:open="${#slNav.current('/build')}"`). The sections are no
pages of their own: the whole row opens and closes. At the top, the application's name and version and a search
field. On a desktop the trigger moves the sidebar out of view; on a phone it opens the same sidebar as a panel.
Switch the preview to Phone to see it.

**Example: Collapsible sub-menus.** A sidebar of sections that open and close, each with its pages in a sub-menu; only the current page's section is open. The trigger moves the sidebar out of view on a desktop and opens it as a panel on a phone.

For reference: the [shadcn/ui block](https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks/sidebar#sidebar-05) this layout is based on. Its
plus and minus are Shadleaf's turning chevron here.

### The layout

The whole layout file. It has what [every layout needs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#what-every-layout-needs): the
theme script and Shadleaf's assets in the head, the skip link first, one `main` (`<sl:sidebar-inset>`), the page's
title, and the toaster.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:fragment="layout(pageTitle, breadcrumb, content)">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title th:text="${pageTitle}">Page</title>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: theme-script}"></th:block>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: assets}"></th:block>
  <link rel="stylesheet" th:href="@{/css/application.css}">
</head>
<body>
```

### A page

A page passes its title, its breadcrumb's levels and its content. The levels are a `th:block` with `th:ref`, so
nothing of it is rendered where it stands; the layout puts them in its `<sl:breadcrumb-list>`.

```html
<html xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:replace="~{layout/main :: layout('Data Fetching', ~{::breadcrumb}, ~{::#page-content})}">
<body>
<th:block th:ref="breadcrumb">
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-link th:href="@{/build}">Build Your Application</sl:breadcrumb-link>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
  <sl:breadcrumb-separator/>
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-page>Data Fetching</sl:breadcrumb-page>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
</th:block>
<div id="page-content">
  ...
</div>
</body>
</html>
```

### The CSS

Shadleaf's CSS styles the components, not the page around them, and has no utility classes. The rest is the
application's CSS, here without Tailwind: the square behind the logo, the magnifier in the search field, a border
below the header, and the page's padding.

```css
/* The square behind the logo in the sidebar's header. */
.app-logo {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  inline-size: 2rem;
  block-size: 2rem;
  border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px);
  background: var(--sidebar-primary);
  color: var(--sidebar-primary-foreground);
}
.app-logo > svg { inline-size: 1rem; block-size: 1rem; }

/* The search field: a magnifier inside it, at the start. */
.docs-search { position: relative; }
.docs-search > .input {
  block-size: 2rem;
  padding-inline-start: 2rem;
  background: var(--background);
}
.docs-search > svg {
  position: absolute;
  inset-inline-start: 0.5rem;
  inset-block-start: 50%;
  translate: 0 -50%;
  inline-size: 1rem;
  block-size: 1rem;
  opacity: 0.5;
  pointer-events: none;
}

/* A border below the page's header, and the page's padding. */
.sidebar-inset > .site-header { border-block-end: 1px solid var(--border); }
.page { padding: 1rem; }
.page > h1 { margin-block-end: 1rem; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; }
```

---

## Collapses to icons

> A team switcher, collapsible sections and projects beside the page, collapsing to a strip of icons on a desktop, with the page as a card and the signed-in user's menu at the bottom.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/collapses-to-icons/

A sidebar for an application with more pages than fit in a header row. At the top, a team switcher: a
[dropdown menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/dropdown-menu.md#opened-from-the-sidebar) opened from a large menu button. Then the
platform's sections as [collapsible items](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md#collapsible-groups), each with its pages in a
sub-menu, the projects with a "More" menu each, and at the bottom the [user menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/user-menu.md). The
page is a card beside the sidebar (`variant="inset"`). The page's header is a
[site header](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/site-header.md) with the trigger, a separator, the page's
[breadcrumb](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/breadcrumb.md) and the theme toggle.

On a desktop the trigger (or Ctrl/⌘+B) collapses the sidebar to a strip of icons (`collapsible="icon"`), with a
tooltip on every menu button, and a cookie remembers the choice. The projects have no icons worth a strip of their
own, so their group is left out of it (`icon-hidden`). On a phone the trigger opens the same sidebar as a panel.
Switch the preview to Phone to see it.

**Example: Collapses to icons.** A team switcher at the top, the platform's sections as collapsible items, projects with a menu each, the signed-in user's menu at the bottom, and the page as a card beside it. On a desktop the trigger collapses the sidebar to a strip of icons with tooltips; on a phone it opens it as a panel.

For reference: the [shadcn/ui block](https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks/sidebar#sidebar-07) this layout is based on.

### The layout

The whole layout file. It has what [every layout needs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#what-every-layout-needs).
The first sample application (sample-01) has a shorter version of it, with its own pages and no team switcher.
`hx-boost` on the body loads every page with htmx; see [With htmx](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#with-htmx) for
the one check a controller then needs. Leave out the script and the attribute for a layout without htmx.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>

      th:fragment="layout(pageTitle, breadcrumb, content)">

  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title th:text="${pageTitle}">Page</title>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: theme-script}"></th:block>
  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: assets}"></th:block>
  <script th:src="@{/webjars/htmx.org/dist/htmx.min.js}" defer></script>
  <link rel="stylesheet" th:href="@{/css/application.css}">
</head>
<body hx-boost="true">
<sl:skip-link/>

        <sl:dropdown-menu-separator/>

    </sl:sidebar-footer>
  </sl:sidebar>
  <sl:sidebar-inset>
    <sl:site-header>
      <sl:sidebar-trigger/>
      <sl:separator orientation="vertical"/>
      <sl:breadcrumb>
        <sl:breadcrumb-list>
          <th:block th:replace="${breadcrumb}"></th:block>
        </sl:breadcrumb-list>
      </sl:breadcrumb>
      <sl:slot name="end"><sl:theme-toggle/></sl:slot>
    </sl:site-header>
    <div class="page">
      <h1 th:text="${pageTitle}"></h1>
      <div th:replace="${content}"></div>
    </div>
  </sl:sidebar-inset>
</sl:sidebar-provider>
<div id="modal-root"></div>
<sl:toaster>
  <sl:toast th:each="toast : ${toasts}" th:title="${toast.title}" th:description="${toast.description}"
            th:variant="${toast.variant}" th:duration="${toast.duration}"/>
</sl:toaster>
</body>
</html>
```

The teams are links, and the server checks the current one (`checked`), so the switcher works without JavaScript; an
application sets it with `th:checked` and lists its teams with `th:each`. The projects' menus are links too: a delete
link leads to a page (or, with htmx, an [alert dialog](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/alert-dialog.md)) that asks first.

Without `variant="inset"` the sidebar is a column along the edge of the screen; with `collapsible="offcanvas"` it
moves out of view instead of collapsing to icons. The [Sidebar](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md) page has every part and
option.

### A page

A page passes its title, its breadcrumb's levels and its content. The levels are a `th:block` with `th:ref`, so
nothing of it is rendered where it stands; the layout puts them in its `<sl:breadcrumb-list>`.

```html
<html xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:replace="~{layout/main :: layout('History', ~{::breadcrumb}, ~{::#page-content})}">
<body>
<th:block th:ref="breadcrumb">
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>Playground</sl:breadcrumb-item>
  <sl:breadcrumb-separator/>
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-page>History</sl:breadcrumb-page>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
</th:block>
<div id="page-content">
  ...
</div>
</body>
</html>
```

### The CSS

Shadleaf's CSS styles the components, not the page around them, and has no utility classes. The rest is the
application's CSS, here without Tailwind: the square behind the logo and the page's padding.

```css
/* The square behind the team's logo in the sidebar's header. */
.app-logo {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  inline-size: 2rem;
  block-size: 2rem;
  border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px);
  background: var(--sidebar-primary);
  color: var(--sidebar-primary-foreground);
}
.app-logo > svg { inline-size: 1rem; block-size: 1rem; }

/* The page's padding: the header above it has its own. */
.page { padding: 0 1rem 1rem; }
.page > h1 { margin-block-end: 1rem; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; }
```

---

## Inset with secondary navigation

> Sections that are pages of their own with a chevron for their sub-menus, projects, a secondary navigation and the user menu, beside the page as a card.

Source: https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/layouts/inset-secondary-navigation/

A sidebar whose sections are pages of their own: the section's name is a link, and a chevron beside it opens and
closes its pages in a [collapsible sub-menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/sidebar.md#a-section-that-is-a-page-too). The server
opens the current page's section. Below them the projects, each with a "More" menu, and at the bottom of the content
a secondary navigation (Support, Feedback) in small buttons. The footer holds the
[user menu](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/user-menu.md). The page is a card beside the sidebar (`variant="inset"`), and its header
has the trigger, the [breadcrumb](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/breadcrumb.md) and the theme toggle. On a desktop the trigger moves
the sidebar out of view; on a phone it opens the same sidebar as a panel. Switch the preview to Phone to see it.

**Example: Inset with secondary navigation.** Sections that are pages of their own, with a chevron beside each that opens its sub-menu, projects with a menu each, a secondary navigation at the bottom and the signed-in user's menu, and the page as a card beside it.

For reference: the [shadcn/ui block](https://ui.shadcn.com/blocks/sidebar#sidebar-08) this layout is based on.

### The layout

The whole layout file. It has what [every layout needs](https://shadleaf.dev/0.11.0-SNAPSHOT/components/application-shell.md#what-every-layout-needs): the
theme script and Shadleaf's assets in the head, the skip link first, one `main` (`<sl:sidebar-inset>`), the page's
title, and the toaster. The chevrons are `summary` elements and need a name each (`aria-label`), as an icon button
does: "Playground's pages".

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:fragment="layout(pageTitle, breadcrumb, content)">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title th:text="${pageTitle}">Page</title>

  <th:block th:replace="~{sl/layout :: assets}"></th:block>
  <link rel="stylesheet" th:href="@{/css/application.css}">
</head>
<body>
<sl:skip-link/>
<sl:sidebar-provider>
  <sl:sidebar variant="inset">
    <sl:sidebar-header>
      <sl:sidebar-menu>
        <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/}" size="lg">
            <sl:slot name="icon-start"><span class="app-logo"><sl:icon name="command"/></span></sl:slot>
            <strong>Acme Inc</strong>
            <small>Enterprise</small>
          </sl:sidebar-menu-button>
        </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
      </sl:sidebar-menu>
    </sl:sidebar-header>
    <sl:sidebar-content>
      <sl:sidebar-group id="nav-platform">
        <sl:sidebar-group-label>Platform</sl:sidebar-group-label>
        <sl:sidebar-menu>
          <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/playground}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/playground', true)}">
              <sl:slot name="icon-start"><sl:icon name="square-terminal"/></sl:slot>
              Playground
            </sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-sub collapsible th:open="${#slNav.current('/playground')}" aria-label="Playground's pages">
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/playground/history}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/playground/history')}">History</sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/playground/starred}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/playground/starred')}">Starred</sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/playground/settings}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/playground/settings')}">Settings</sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-sub>
          </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/models}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/models', true)}">

              Models
            </sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-sub collapsible th:open="${#slNav.current('/models')}" aria-label="Models's pages">
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/models/genesis}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/models/genesis')}">Genesis</sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/models/explorer}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/models/explorer')}">Explorer</sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>

              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-sub>
          </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
          <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/docs}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/docs', true)}">
              <sl:slot name="icon-start"><sl:icon name="book-open"/></sl:slot>
              Documentation
            </sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-sub collapsible th:open="${#slNav.current('/docs')}" aria-label="Documentation's pages">

              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/settings/team}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/settings/team')}">Team</sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/settings/billing}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/settings/billing')}">Billing</sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
              <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
                <sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button th:href="@{/settings/limits}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/settings/limits')}">Limits</sl:sidebar-menu-sub-button>
              </sl:sidebar-menu-sub-item>
            </sl:sidebar-menu-sub>
          </sl:sidebar-menu-item>
        </sl:sidebar-menu>
      </sl:sidebar-group>
      <sl:sidebar-group id="nav-projects">
        <sl:sidebar-group-label>Projects</sl:sidebar-group-label>
        <sl:sidebar-menu>
          <sl:sidebar-menu-item>
            <sl:sidebar-menu-button th:href="@{/projects/design}" th:active="${#slNav.current('/projects/design')}">
              <sl:slot name="icon-start"><sl:icon name="frame"/></sl:slot>
              Design Engineering
            </sl:sidebar-menu-button>

                  <sl:icon name="folder"/>
                  View project
                </sl:dropdown-menu-item>

              Sales &amp; Marketing
            </sl:sidebar-menu-button>
            <sl:dropdown-menu id="project-sales-more">
              <sl:dropdown-menu-trigger as="sidebar-menu-action" show-on-hover aria-label="More for Sales &amp; Marketing">

                </sl:dropdown-menu-item>

        <sl:dropdown-menu-separator/>

        <sl:dropdown-menu-item as="a" th:href="@{/billing}"><sl:icon name="credit-card"/>Billing</sl:dropdown-menu-item>
        <sl:dropdown-menu-item as="a" th:href="@{/notifications}"><sl:icon name="bell"/>Notifications</sl:dropdown-menu-item>
      </sl:user-menu>
    </sl:sidebar-footer>
  </sl:sidebar>
  <sl:sidebar-inset>
    <sl:site-header>
      <sl:sidebar-trigger/>
      <sl:separator orientation="vertical"/>
      <sl:breadcrumb>
        <sl:breadcrumb-list>
          <th:block th:replace="${breadcrumb}"></th:block>
        </sl:breadcrumb-list>
      </sl:breadcrumb>
    <sl:slot name="end"><sl:theme-toggle/></sl:slot>
    </sl:site-header>
    <div class="page">
      <h1 th:text="${pageTitle}"></h1>
      <div th:replace="${content}"></div>
    </div>
  </sl:sidebar-inset>
</sl:sidebar-provider>
<div id="modal-root"></div>
<sl:toaster>
  <sl:toast th:each="toast : ${toasts}" th:title="${toast.title}" th:description="${toast.description}"
            th:variant="${toast.variant}" th:duration="${toast.duration}"/>
</sl:toaster>
</body>
</html>
```

### A page

A page passes its title, its breadcrumb's levels and its content. The levels are a `th:block` with `th:ref`, so
nothing of it is rendered where it stands; the layout puts them in its `<sl:breadcrumb-list>`.

```html
<html xmlns:th="http://www.thymeleaf.org" xmlns:sl="https://shadleaf.dev/sl"
      th:replace="~{layout/main :: layout('History', ~{::breadcrumb}, ~{::#page-content})}">
<body>
<th:block th:ref="breadcrumb">
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-link th:href="@{/playground}">Playground</sl:breadcrumb-link>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
  <sl:breadcrumb-separator/>
  <sl:breadcrumb-item>
    <sl:breadcrumb-page>History</sl:breadcrumb-page>
  </sl:breadcrumb-item>
</th:block>
<div id="page-content">
  ...
</div>
</body>
</html>
```

### The CSS

Shadleaf's CSS styles the components, not the page around them, and has no utility classes. The rest is the
application's CSS, here without Tailwind: the square behind the logo, the secondary navigation pushed to the bottom
of the content (the `nav-secondary` class on its group), and the page's padding.

```css
/* The square behind the logo in the sidebar's header. */
.app-logo {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  flex-shrink: 0;
  inline-size: 2rem;
  block-size: 2rem;
  border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px);
  background: var(--sidebar-primary);
  color: var(--sidebar-primary-foreground);
}
.app-logo > svg { inline-size: 1rem; block-size: 1rem; }

/* The secondary navigation at the bottom of the sidebar's content. */
.nav-secondary { margin-block-start: auto; }

/* The page's padding: the header above it has its own. */
.page { padding: 0 1rem 1rem; }
.page > h1 { margin-block-end: 1rem; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 600; }
```
